title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] Heat. Heat. Hey. Hey. Hey. >> [music] >> Heat. Heat. 3. >> Dick. Heat. >> I'm happy. >> Donald's >> Heat. Wow. Heat. Heat. N. Down. I don't think >> Oh, Hey, feel free. Everything. >> Down. Now let's see. Heat up here. All right. Uh, quick turnaround. Um, I guess that's the beauty of having the short week is we got to launch right into Packers. um an exciting opportunity for us and um you know we kind of said what we needed to say in the locker room and a lot of things were you talked about um between myself the coaches connecting with the players you know just but wanting to make sure we're able to move forward um to have the type of day we did today which is full focus Packers here we go >> Dave did have surgery and is he out for the year >> he will have surgery um you know he's got he's got a uh a fracture in his fibula up high kind of right below the knee, but it was really the ankle that got damaged the most with ligaments and all that. So, um he'll have a procedure and that'll put him out for the rest of the year. >> That will the procedure be on his ankle? >> Yes. >> What What can you say about the guy who gone through the clots and come back and now this >> I know I just really like myself, his teammates, you know, we're all hurt for Teemo. Um, but we know what he represents and and uh how he battled to get back out there and and in the process was just available to his teammates, you know, and um and a guy like Monroe Freeling, you know, who needed that uh sounding board as he was out there, you know, playing early and and now he's going to come back in there. Um but, you know, just again for the last couple of weeks as he's been out there and available for us, you know, to feel the joy and the and the gratitude uh coming out of Teemo. Um it was a great thing for us. It was a great thing for the team. um as you get into the season, as you start to one practice after the other and you have that mentality, when somebody comes out there with that kind of uh approach and that kind of attitude, it just adds a spark and I really appreciate Teemo for bringing that. >> Dave, when you watch the film, whatever amount of film that you watched after the short [clears throat] >> Yeah, I watched it a lot. you know, I watched uh watched the whole game uh all the way through and then, you know, went back and threw on the run game, you know, and our defense playing against it and a great uh a great performance by the Bucks, but you know, giving them their due with the plan that they had and how they executed and then looking at what we can do better. And that's what we're focused on, you know, um, as a staff with our players as well is as we go into this week, while we can't necessarily just take all those clips and spend all that time looking at through the game, we can certainly look at the Packers, what they might try to do to emulate some of the things that were successful and have a plan and be ready for that. >> Dave, you've said in the past that [clears throat] you back this scheme because you've seen it at its best and play well, but also over the last three years, you've given up more than 200 rushing yards in 12 games. The only common denominator really there is scheme. What is the issue with this run defense when you guys are struggling? >> And that's what we're working on right now. You know, I don't really want to get into the specifics of it. I feel like there's, you know, the adjustments and the things that we need to do. I don't want to really air that out, but um just understanding that we got to do it. We got to execute it well um together. We got to coach it better uh collectively. We got to have that plan. Um so that when it becomes the the same type of concepts that our players feel prepared, they feel ready to attack whatever it is. Let's take this run out of it. They're going to have to go to these other ones, you know, and so that's what we've been working through. Um talking through >> guys have said in the to follow up on that, sorry. >> Yeah. >> Guys have said in the locker room that they knew that the Bucks were going to run it against you guys. Uh that would seem to be a spot where Lean Ransom could could make a difference there. He did not play very much up until the game was out of hand. What's going into like the personnel issues on the back end, especially with all these injuries? >> Yeah, I mean, that's a possibility. Lean's done a great job um showing up for us with physicality and, you know, we missed a couple of tackles. Um but again, it's about reducing space. It's about showing up where you need to, hitting blocks, right? Um guys that are have a single, being able to get off those blocks and disrupt it, you know. Um, so, you know, there's there's optionality from a personnel standpoint, but there's optionality as well with what our concepts are and how we're how we're deploying them. So, we got to take all those things into consideration though, uh, given the fact that yes, you know, this was a game where we felt like, hey, are they going to really put the ball in Baker's hands, which Baker did a phenomenal job of just finding some wins and he's scrappy. We know that. Um, but at the same time, you know, they were they had a mode, they had a plan. Um and uh we got to make sure that another team doesn't feel like they can come in and execute that type of plan. >> Where is um at right now as far as his rehab? You told us a couple weeks ago there was a ways to go. >> Yeah, I mean just every week seems like good milestones. Um good progression. I can't tell you exactly how close that is, how far that is. Um but I know that he's trending in the right direction. Um getting into some more individual drills where he can start to really load and anchor and do all those things. But um it's got to get to a point where we feel really comfortable about, you know, sending somebody at him full speed and do all that. We're not quite there yet, you know, so um I can't really tell you specifically. >> And then yesterday with special teams, what did you see when looking back on lock point and also last week you had Trevor back there return was there for the month. What led to the decision to have him back there Trevor? >> We actually had Demo in the same spot uh the last two weeks. um those logo punts kind of making those decisions backed up inside of the 15 inside of the 10 yard line. So um gave him Demo a guy I really trust, a guy that we've trusted for a long time. Um one of our best catchers there, you know, put the ball on the ground, you know. Um but you know, Trevor has done a good job catching at midfield. We have to evaluate that part as well. That's our job is okay, like who's going to give us the best chance to be successful there. Dave, kind of building off of uh Mike's question about personnel, defensive backs, uh what does Shaw Smith Wade need to do to get more chances? >> Just opportunity, you know. Um we put A Caleb back out there uh for another game and you know, he had he had really tight coverage on a pass interference. I thought it was a good call, you know. Um I think it was uh was it Ted was the receiver on that one? >> Yeah, Ted. And uh he did a great job playing back into him, but Caleb had tight coverage on that play. uh the scramble play touchdown, you know, he kind of lost uh I think it was Johnson in the back half, you know, he kind of lost him late on the scramble. Baker does a great job buying time. We got heat on him. Trey's right there, you know, and he makes a great throw. Um but I thought, you know, I thought AK was doing a great job in terms of just stepping in there in a time that we really needed him and uh you know, Shaw get his opportunity at some point, you know, but again, we have to take all these things into consideration how we're using guys in other phases as well. >> So you guys sticking with Evans this week? Evans is dayto-day right now, so we got to see some major progression on a short week. Um, he's got a he's got an arm tricep injury, so we're going to have to evaluate that as a coach. >> With Cory Thordon in OTAAS, you were talking about how much promise he had and how much he I mean, how he won the job mid year at Nickel. Now he's been on the practice squad, hasn't been elevated with all these injuries. What's his outlook with the organization right now? >> Cory's doing a great job. He's doing everything we ask him to do. He does have versatility. Um, you know, and the the thing we have to evaluate is who gives us the best opportunity to win outside, to be at the corner spot, you know, exclusively, um, without some of that other flexibility knowing that we have guys that are doing that role for us pretty well right now. So, um, but yeah, I mean, basic comment on Cory, like he's he's busting his butt every day. Um, he's ready if we need him. >> If can't go, who would it be? >> I don't want to say that right now. Um, we're going to go dayto-day with AK and then and then, uh, we got options, you know. Um, Malcolm showed up on the practice squad. He's a gunner. Uh, Marco Wilson's been on our practice squad. Uh, doing some good things. Cory, guys mentioned Cory. So, we do have options. I'm glad we have these guys that have been around so that we can train them. Um, and and we'll go from there. >> Guys like Bobby Brown. >> Yeah, Bobb's >> Bobby's got a hand dayto day. Uh, we'll evaluate that. Who else? Uh, Jaylen. Jaylen Phillips. Yeah, we're going to try we're going to try to get him back for this game, but again, the recurring same hamstring, you know, it's still that kind of a tight window, so it'll be close on that one. >> And Damian Yeah, Damen's got a knee right now. Um, he'll be dayto-day uh just to see if we can get him back. So, >> what's that? >> Oh, sorry. >> Going back to the run defense stuff, you talk about the adjustments needing to be made this week. It is a short week. Don't get me on the field as much. I'm just curious, are you wanting guys to do that more in the film room? Is this on their own? Is it like blocking stuff out in the hotel room? Like what does that kind of look like on a short week? >> It's the whole group. Um, it's the coaching staff, it's the players, it's being on the same page and understanding who this offense is, what the formations are, what the types of runs that could possibly be out there so that we have a level of anticipation that helps the execution, but it does come down to making sure we're fitting our blocks properly, making sure the support's showing up to force it when they do, and maintaining leverage. Um, you know, they got they bounced a couple on us, you know, and got to the sideline. Our defense is designed for that to not happen. So, we have to reduce that space and that comes from taking all the information and so um and that's all of our responsibility really. >> D coming into a week when you guys have a winning record u you guys over the past couple years have not been able to sustain I guess success moving into the new weeks. I believe it's 0 and six over the past few years. Um what do you kind of attribute that to in terms of being able to sustain while also knowing it's a week to week? Yeah, I got to take responsibility of that for preparing my team to have the mindset to be able to handle that success and to understand you can't change your process, but the more that we continue to improve as a team, you're going to get a better shot from the team you're playing. And you know, I know what that feels like in different ways to be on a team that a team kind of sleeps on you, you know, and they didn't expect what you brought. And then to be on the flip side of it where everybody's trying to beat you, everybody's trying to, you know, show what they can do. Not that it necessarily becomes all about you, but that's a factor. It's a dynamic, you know, and that's something that, um, I've spent a lot of time thinking about, talking to people about of how to prepare our guys so that one, the process and preparation doesn't Wayne, doesn't relax. It stays focused and engaged. And even more so now, guys, even more so, this urgency is even greater knowing the Bucks coming in having struggles, a division opponent, and really playing with great energy. And I thought our guys played hard. I I knew we played with great energy and all that, but we have to be ready and focused to be able to execute at the basic level. Um, expecting those type of a match match up. To follow up on that, >> we're gonna do this one, then we're going to do Hulk, and then we're [clears throat] >> you guys are like eight and three after losses since last year. >> How do knowing that you've had that success, why do you think there's a disconnect the opposite way around? And like how do you kind of hone in on like what's working off the losses as opposed to the wins? >> And that's something to be proud of, but that's also the urgency that we're talking about. And um I think we all know like when you face situations where um you have this challenge in front of you and it puts us in a in a in a state of mind where this play right now in practice is so urgent. This these days stacking up a great week is so urgent right now. And the feeling that you're left with, you know, after a loss when you're going when you're coming out of a win, you got to be able to create. We I have to be able to create the same type of urgency from the group to say, "Now look what we're now look where we're headed. Can we find better ball than we had last week? Can we have that same fight, that same urgency, that same getting out of the mud type of mentality, you know, where um and be comfortable with that, you know, and I mean, it made me think about, you know, uh the game last night and just uh two amazing teams, you know, who really regard and respect each other and the type of preparation it takes, you know, to for the Seahawks defense to hold a really a really powerful offense, you know, three points. Both teams having that mutual respect. We have to be able to go into every week with that same regard, you know, and not just get up for certain games, you know, but have consistency about it because it's about us and it's about us pursuing our best. That should be enough. Let's get together on that same mindset so we can make that happen. >> Last one from Hulk. >> On the lighter side, Anthony Tyus, he was all smiles in the locker room after the game. He was a blowout loss, end of a game, but he still scored his first NFL touchdown coming through on special teams and then the score. What does it say about an undrafted free agent M guy just getting his opportunity? >> Yeah, just grit um trusting the whole process and development of what we're doing here and uh finding a way to help his teammates however it's possible. finding a way to help his team. Um whether it's covering kicks, whether it's attacking punts, returning, you know, and then I love that he got some opportunities at the end. I hate that we were in that mode, but we were. And uh so it's still great football for us to evaluate. It's it was still important to all of us to continue to just call these plays and execute and finish regardless of what the score says. We got to just keep playing ball and doing things right. And I was glad that Trey got in there and was able to get in the end zone. >> Last one. We've seen Bryce face pressure pretty much all year and before yesterday it kind of thrived with it or thrived in the face of it and then it became a little catastrophic yesterday. What can you and Brad do to to kind of avoid that going forward, especially with the rework line? >> Yeah, just giving him uh quick availability in one way, shape, or form. However you're building your formations, making sure somebody's looking at them. Um just knowing and especially this week um Jonathan Ganon does a great job with different packages, show packages where they drop out then they come and looking to be aggressive and multiple and exotic. So um just making sure we build somebody in there that's got their eyes back at Bryce because he does a great job of getting the ball uh to guys in voids and so um and he's been having success with it. I think the last couple of weeks, you know, um you know, it's been a little bit of a challenge, you know, to get those completions versus pressure, but um it's something that he's excelled in. So, I think it's it's kind of just building those things and uh giving him some quicker options. Even when you do have an element that stretches the field, that's what we want. You know, when when the protection allows it, we can still take advantage of those uh shot plays, but let's give him an early option so that he has somewhere to go with it, too. >> All right. Thanks, >> Yep. All right. Thank you. >> Hallelujah.

title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes & Chris Jones Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 7
text: All right, really not anything injury wise to mention. Nick had some spasms in his neck and he'll work through that and he'll be good. Listen, all all three phases we struggled. So, we've got to do better as a and that's my responsibility. So, I take full responsibility for this. We've got a we've got to play better as a team. A tough place to play, but this is all part of it. They got a good football team and they they played well. My hat goes off to them. There's not a whole lot of stats that I can share with you that really make any sense maybe other than third downs both sides of the ball. We we can do a better job with those, but we've got a great locker room here and guys will get back in and get themselves ready to play against a good Denver team this next week. So, with that time's yours. >> What enabled them to sort of stifle the run and the pass? That's cuz you guys present a lot of complications for most teams. >> Yeah, I'll take responsibility for that. Putting guys in the right position to to make plays. So, you know, they they they did. They did a great job both both areas and um you know, we'll get better at it. We just got to go back to the drawing board here a little bit. >> I know I know you have faith in Harrison, but it looked like he left one short, which is a little uncharacteristic of him. Is there anything going wrong with him physically or >> all three all three phases with the with the everybody had their you know, had had an issue starting with me. So, it's uh we all had a piece of that. >> Andy, how much did the the pressure disrupt what you were trying to do offensively? >> Yeah, I mean they they did a good job defensively. I mean they they had pressure. Um so, we can do better better versus that. again, some of it's play calls And we'll take care of that. >> Follow up on Harrison. What what's your concern level with with that right now? >> Yeah, I mean, listen, he's been one of the most consistent kickers in football, but um he's off a bit. So, got to fix it. >> And then defensively, what there were a lot of like between third and five and third and 10s, did you I obviously if you saw the common denominator you would have fixed it, but what what what stuck out to you about how we >> Yeah, you got to keep yourself, especially against this this group here. Yeah, you got to keep yourself out of third and long situations. And that's you got to do better on first and second down. So, we we can we can do better. We had some penalties in there also that got got us going the wrong direction um when we were moving the ball and you got to take care of those. >> Any particular message you you leave the team with after a game like this? >> Yeah, we've got to learn from it. Well, I you know, I mentioned to you guys before, win or lose, you got to learn and get better. And so, we'll do that. I'll start with myself and uh we'll work our way through it and make sure that we we teach and uh and you got to have the right locker room to handle that and I've I feel like I've got a a great locker room. So, um they'll take care of business here. >> Can you wonder if you can comment on anything on the Josh Simmons report about the meeting at all? >> Yeah, listen, Sam, I I've said I've said so much on him. Rex talked about him this and that. Things happen and uh that's not that's no reason that it uh he was put on IR. He's got a bad back. And so, um he's got to get that worked out and that's uh the main thing. But, that's all. Leave it at that. I mean, that's where we're at with >> Okay, yes. Thank you. [clears throat] >> All right. >> Overall, >> Yeah, I mean, got your got your tail kicked. Didn't execute offensively especially especially around that midfield area. Kept us away from a lot of points or at least enough points to be competitive. but it's stuff you got to learn from. That's obviously a really good defense and we didn't execute at a high enough level to have success. >> One of the things you guys have been able to do is present enough options to make it difficult for a team to stop at all but it seemed like they pretty effective on all aspects of the game. >> Yeah, they they did a great job. You know, that they they passed off their zones. They played man when they needed to play man. And then they got us off the field on third down. We moved the ball a little bit kind of in between like where you get it from kickoff to the midfield but in order to have success in this league you got to be able to sustain drives and we weren't weren't able to do that and obviously they contained the explosive plays. So it's stuff that we have to continue to get better at. And you can't have those mistakes versus defense. >> How much did their pressure really affect what you guys wanted to do? >> Yeah, I mean obviously a little bit but I thought especially early in the game I thought my feet were were kind of getting me into trouble where I could have maybe sat in the pocket and made some of the throws down the field. I got better a little bit later in the game but at the same time whenever you play a a team like that you can't let them get ahead and kind of get into a game they want to play cuz obviously they've had a lot of success doing that and so got to be better starting faster especially with me and then try to do better throughout the entire game. >> What did you see on just on the interception? >> Yeah, I mean obviously I was trying to make the throw. Kind of really had two guys in the area but I was really trying to throw it to 11. Got kind of pulled down as I was throwing it and it sailed high over the top of his head. You don't want to put the ball in harm's way especially in that midfield area. Believe on second down so just just trying to find a way to get either get the ball to him and make a throw or throw the ball away. So I got to be better there. >> After you get good sense >> What what's what's the takeaway you want the guys to have from this game? >> Yeah, I mean I think the biggest takeaway is if you don't come ready to play is just you can get your tail kicked in this league and no matter if you're 5 and 0 or whatever it is, like it's every week's a new week and every team can do this. And so you have to have that mindset of when you go throughout the week of practice of we need our best football that Sunday and I have to do the same as well. And so we got a young team. It'll be about how we respond from this. Obviously with the big game coming up this next week. So let's get let's get rolling and and get ourselves ready for that. >> Is that something you're saying based on just moving forward or something you're saying based on reflecting on the last week? >> No, I think it was just moving forward, you know, you never know. I mean you we've we've played in some primetime games, but they all can go so many different ways. And so like I said it's a young team. It's a learning experience. But for us veteran guys, we got to show them how we respond from this. I think that that'll be the biggest thing is that just like how this game went, we can go out there and play better the next week. In this league it's week to week and it's about going out there and having a great week of practice and getting ourselves prepared for another great defense. >> It's a little bit related Patrick, but you've had a little bit of a history of you know, when you've had a game like this like surging kind of afterwards. What in your mind what's the key to that transformation and >> I mean >> Same thing you said? >> I think I think the biggest thing is like you I mean you got to feel it. I mean this is this sucks. You don't you want you don't want to perform like this in primetime and a big big moment like this. So you got to feel it on that plane right home and and understand that it sucks. But then how how can you build off of it? Like that's the biggest thing is as we get back and and get get back to that film study on the Broncos, you got to see where you made your mistakes and how they're going to try to execute and then do stuff to combat that and play better. And so obviously it sucks right now, but we'll be we'll be full steam ahead trying to do our our best to find a way to win this next week. >> We've seen K9 be such a difference maker for you guys, but from your perspective, what did they do to really lock down the running game? >> Yeah, I mean we have to help him. I think that's the The thing is when they put um many eggs in that in that basket of stopping the run game, we have to have the play-action game and the movement game to be able to to throw the ball. Um and if we're not proving that, they're going to continue to put those put those guys up at the line of scrimmage. And then and that that's hard for the run game. And he made the most of the what the opportunities that he had, but for me having some of those play actions early in the game, if I can hit some of those, um it'll loosen up the defense and then he can kind of get going. And that's what we've been so good at this year. And obviously we didn't do it this year uh this game. >> Patrick, pre-snap it looked like you were doing a lot of moving people around, trying to get people in the right spot. Was that crowd noise thing, or was that just maybe guys just not being on the right right page at the right time? >> Yeah, I mean, just it Like I said, it's a young team and just trying to communicate and make sure everybody's on the same page. And we made our mistakes here and there, but I thought I was proud of how the guys fought at the end um in that second half. Obviously we didn't play and score touchdowns. The guys were were were fighting to make plays happen. And so we'll learn from this. Um and we'll we'll be better from it. >> Okay, thanks, Patrick. And then Don Payne defensively? >> It's a lot of things we could have done better. I think we gave up a 21-yard run. Um a few more stops on third down that we we let slip on us. Um I think more so just watching the film and being critical of yourself as a player, as an individual, then also as a whole as a defense as a whole, our offense as a whole. >> How difficult is it to to bring down Sam? I I know he's getting away from the [snorts and clears throat] pocket and you had a couple chances with him escaping. I guess just how how much of a challenge was that ended up being today? >> I think we got to do a better job as a D-line as in um closing the pocket, um filling those voids to making sure he's he doesn't have an escape lane. I think we didn't do such a good job today because he was able to make a third down, once again, a a positive yard gain. So I think that's something we can look at film and we can correct. Um just watching film more so, watch film, correct the errors that we made, and get ready and prepare for Denver. >> Anybody else? >> Chris, had you a particular message for the young guys offensively, defensively? Any Any message going forward after this one? >> Oh. Like it's just like a little adversity in life. You know, you're going to face adversity at some point in time in life. You know, we all have aspirations of want to go undefeated. You know, that's always the goal. And sometimes you face adversity and you know, it's a point in time you're going to face it, but it's about how you how how you come back. Cuz you're going to face it at some point in time in some some area in your life adversity is going to hit you. It's about how you bounce back. So, I think we got the guys on this team with a lot of high character that we've been in this situation before. You know, you go back to last year and then you fast forward to where we are now. We're sitting 5 and 1 and it is It's a lot of good going into that, but you know, for us I think it's more specific um correcting our errors and being prepared for for Denver coming up. >> What What's Coach Reed's message after after a game like this in the locker room and and how do you guys move forward you know, from that? >> Just correct our errors in all phases of the game. I think this was a game where we um >> [clears throat] >> we we we we struggled in all phases as a as a team. As a team, special teams, offense, defense. It's not no one particular area. And I think we can bounce back as a team also. You know, have a great week of practice. Preparation is always key and look forward for the upcoming opponent. >> Thank you everybody. Thank you. >> Thank you Coach. Thank you.

title: LIVE: Houston Texans EVP & GM Nick Caserio addresses the media
text: I was lucky. Good morning.  I am grateful to everyone who has gathered here.  Uh, yeah, I... I mean, I'm ready for questions. So, uh, you know, we have two and five, we have what we have. Of course, we can play better.  Uh, you know, of course, we can do a lot of things better, uh, together.  Uh, you know, including myself . So, uh, let's try to use this week off, look at some of the things that, you know, we're doing well. Let's look at some areas where we can improve.  Some of them, to be honest, I don't want to oversimplify everything, but I mean , it all comes down to the basics and technique.  I mean, excitement is excitement.  That is, you are either good at excitement or you are not.  I'm for the fact that we can make some changes in terms of yardage in some areas, but, you know, we're one of the teams with the most penalties and one of the worst tackles in the league.  So if we can make incremental progress in some of these aspects, then, you know, that could potentially lead to a better outcome. I mean, the reality is: look, we have two and five.  We lost four games on the last possession .  So, what can we do on the edge of what we can do to potentially improve the situation and see push these games?  We have one and four in games with a difference of one point, or something like that.  We were able to pull out a victory in the game against Jacksonville because we did everything in critical situations. So, this is where we are now.  So there's no point in being sad and, you know, wallowing in self-pity. This is the NFL.  There are a lot of good teams here, a lot of good players.  We can definitely improve a bit.  If we make these improvements, we'll see if the results get better. So I think that's what we'll be focusing on this week.  So, Sarge, I'll open up the opportunity, let you have the first question. Nick, given how the roster is currently structured , excluding injuries, do you think you've put together a successful roster at this point?  Well, I mean, in the offseason you put together the team that you think is most appropriate. So, when the season starts, you know, we try to figure out who maybe needs to play more and who needs to play less. What other different things can we do?  I mean, the team is what it is.  We won't see any significant changes to the lineup until the offseason.  So we will go back and take a look, because that is part of our responsibility. Let's look back, analyze our actions, decisions made , what we could have done a little differently. This is a kind of rewriting of history.  We assembled the team because we thought it was the right decision at the time.  When you make such decisions, you don't really think about what the final result in the table will be. The main thing is to assemble the best team, and then go out and try to play good football.  Sometimes , as a team, we just didn't play as consistently as we would have liked, from start to finish.  We only did it in snippets. The game was a bit disjointed at times.  We need to see if we can play, and we've already talked about this, better team football, complementing each other.  And if we do that, then perhaps the result will be a little different. Again, we were in a situation where we could have won every match except the game against Cincinnati, which was very tough.  In every other game we had a chance to win, but we couldn't take advantage of it.  We must give credit to our opponent.  They made more plays, and look, that's the reality of the NFL.  Sometimes things work out that way Will we see any changes in the lineup? I beg your pardon? Will we see any changes in the lineup? We'll see.  We will look into it.  If they deem it appropriate, then great.  And what is the alternative?  We will analyze everything and will not make hasty decisions immediately after yesterday's events.  We'll go through this week, take stock. We'll spend time with the coaching staff, discuss different things, whether it's schemes or shots, and then try to find the best formula to move forward. Honestly, everything will probably change from week to week because injuries will be a part of it, who's available, who's not, who's coming back, and so on .  So we take the information at that moment and try to make the decision that we think is most logical for that particular week. A little.  Two questions for you.  First, are you surprised by how things have turned out over these eight games?  Regarding your start, two wins and six losses, two and five.  I know we already lost to the Chargers, but that's okay. Listen, our expectations remain the same. We approach this like a league where everything is decided every week. So, who is our opponent?  What should we do this week? And in the end, you either make enough good plays or you don't.  So, I mean , this approach will not change.  So today we're going to look at it the same way we did last week.  So, you either win or you lose. You're trying to figure out what happened during the game.  After all, we can't control everything.  Nobody knows what will happen.  I don't know for sure.  You all probably know what will happen each week.  I definitely don't. You try to put a team together and then you go out and either plays or you don't.    I mean, I don't know how to simplify it, but that's how it is. You mentioned Continue.  He said it.  Second question. You mentioned that you need to get better.  How exactly do you think you should become better and why should this happen? Yes, just making sure we have the right people on the team.  if not, then we have to find other people.  So, again, we talked about the different stages of team formation.  The offseason, March, April, May—this is probably the time when the main work on the composition takes place. So we will always keep an eye on this.  If there's something we can do better, we'll try to figure out if it makes sense.  During the season, it all depends on each week, and the pool of available players may be limited. So you won't be able to radically rebuild your team.  You just try to take the group you have and, you know, do your best, and if it doesn't work, then you have to change course and do something else.  I'm sure there are players who are here now, but they won't be there next season. I mean, it's just part of the cyclical nature of this process.  So, I mean, that's exactly the situation we're in right now. Nick, regarding the offensive line, we talked back in August and you were pretty happy with it.  How would you rate the offensive line's performances compared to what you expected?  And my second question: do you expect to be a buyer or a seller during the trade deadline? Yes, regarding the second question, we will consider every possibility.  If that makes sense—great. If not, we are always open to suggestions.  We have already held negotiations.  We talked, you know, to most of the teams in the league.  Teams started contacting us, trying to find out: well, what's the state of the other teams right now ?  What are you looking for?  Where do you have a surplus of players? Do you know where you potentially have a need? So we will always be impartial.  We are not going to rule anything out.  We will listen and, ultimately, do what we think makes the most sense. Regarding the first part of the question, regarding the offensive line.  It was probably a bit of an ups and downs. Sometimes everything was good.  Sometimes it can be better.  I think we talked about it within the team, and we discussed it at different points.  We just have to finish the blocks better.  We are in touch, and sometimes we are on point, but sometimes we fail to keep it up until the end of the game episode.  So we just need to do a better job of staying in touch and following through .  And again, we have a number of players at that position.  We have 11 offensive linemen on the roster, probably as many as any other team.  So we had guys who got injured and guys who are coming back to play. So we'll look and try to understand: if this is the top five—great. If not, we'll try to do something else.  In terms of the lineup, how you formed it in the offseason, do you think it matches what's happening on the field and the execution of what you're trying to do? Yeah, listen: we've always prided ourselves on trying to play physical football, being, you know, physically tough, trying to win on the line of scrimmage, winning up front, and we felt when we put the team together that we would have the ability to do that.  Um, we fell a little short in some of these games, after all.  So, again , we feel we have enough players who can help us win matches. Again, I don't want to speak for the players, but many of them will probably tell you that they can play better too. They can do their job better.  We have players who individually job quite well.  Collectively, we haven't always done our job as a single unit , and that's probably why we're where we are.  We have certain gaps.  So, you know, we'll see what happens throughout the season. Let's see if we can play together again, as one team. Again, I know we look at it pessimistically, but the reality is we lost four games on the last possession.  So we put ourselves in a position to win these matches.  We just couldn't ultimately do the job well and do enough to win.  So that's the reality.  I don't want to exaggerate, but this is the NFL. Nick, I know you don't like to talk about last year.  However, considering that there were almost no personnel changes in defense.  Why do you think there was such a big decline compared to what you were able to do last year and how the defense is playing this year? Yes, every year is different. One year has no impact on what is happening.  So , the '25 team was the '25 team .  The 2016 team is where we are now.  So there really is no connection between what happened where we are now, other than we didn't play well enough as a team. So, I mean, that's the reality.  If we all looked at ourselves in the mirror, it would be exactly like this. What do you think the defense is not doing to get better? Yes.  Well, again, we're the worst team in the league in terms of making tackles. Too many missed tackles and we allow too many explosive playmaking moments.  So , I mean, take these two aspects.  If we made better tackles and allowed fewer explosive moments, we would see a better result in defense. And intercepting the ball. We didn't really intercept the ball very often.  We do a very good job in attack, keeping the ball. I think we probably have the fewest losses in the league, we're close to that. So, we are doing a good job of possession and taking care of the ball.  But we don't take the ball away from the opponent.  So, we're not making any interceptions, we're missing too many tackles, and we're allowing too many explosive opportunities, so we're probably not playing defense at our level.  You mentioned the players' play and the basics of tackling.  Do you feel that in terms of the scheme you are on par with those you play with on Sundays? As for how the defense is built , there are a lot of free agents, well, the offense doesn't seem to have a face.  It is extremely variable from week to week.  Do you think that schematically, apart from the basics and the players themselves , you are on par? Yes, listen, this is a league where everything changes every week.  So what does the team do, who are we playing against, what are we to defend or what are we playing against offensively? What are we trying to attack?  So, again, we have enough players and enough schemes.  We just need to do our job better, a little better. If we execute the plan better, the outcome may be different. So are you happy with your schemes?  Is that "yes"? I say we have enough schemes. After all, we don't have defensive plays whose purpose is to let the receiver run free, right?  If the defense is calling for pressure and a receiver change at the line of scrimmage, and you don't do that, then we're missing the play .  Okay.  So is this a problem with the scheme?  Is this a player problem?  So, how do offensive coordinators play combinations to get a player free and one step ahead? if there are any specific examples, I have n't seen too many of them, you know, in terms of, here's our draw, here's their combination, we have a plan and everything is taken into account in every draw.  Of course? If we play with the wrong distribution of power, or if we are too far from the receiver, or we don't block him even though we've been practicing it all week, and we let him go on a route , then I don't think it's the result of "the opposing coordinator choosing a good scheme."  We just need to do better at executing what is planned.  Of course, are there any schematic plays that they came up with that allowed them to carry out successful attacks?  Yes, this is the NFL.  There are good coaches here, and there are usually good players.  So, in the end, collectively, if we can all up our game a little bit , then the outcome might be different. There is a perception that since you and C.J. Stroud's representatives couldn't reach an agreement, he essentially took it upon himself. Obviously he has his own point of view, but have you ever had the feeling that he was putting himself at risk by refusing a deal or one of your offers?  I'm not sure I understand the question. OK.  So, I'm just curious.  Did you feel like C.J. Stroud was putting himself at risk by not accepting a deal you might have offered in the offseason? I mean, you can ask CJ what he thinks.  We spent...yes.  No, we had very good negotiations.  I think we were pretty close to the goal.  We were unable to complete the deal.  I don't think anyone is too worried about this .  So I will say that he goes out on the field and, frankly, plays very good football, which is no surprise to anyone .  I think not many people, except maybe Demo and me, supported him throughout the offseason, when he was basically getting mudsled for four months because of, you know, one bad half of a game. So the way he behaves and the way he approaches things is a testament to who he is, and that doesn't surprise any of us.  You know, I think the contract issue will resolve itself, no matter what happens.  So, um, yeah, I mean, we were close to that.  We didn't manage to bring the matter to a conclusion, but I do n't think that will deter anyone from reaching an agreement in the future, whenever that happens. If you knew he would play the way he is playing now, would you have tried to finish the deal before the season started? I think everyone did their best , but, you know, we fell a little short.  So, I repeat, I don't think anyone is surprised by his performance.  I mean, he's a good quarterback.  He's been a good quarterback since he came into the league.  I know sometimes everyone looks at it from a different angle, but the guy has been playing very well since he's been in the league .  This is just reality.  And we've already talked about this.  That's exactly what Demo and I think .  This is what we talked about.  I don't know how many times I've been asked about this , and I've talked about his professionalism, his performance, his attitude and how he worked in the offseason.  I think you see a direct correlation between the work he did in the offseason and the results on the field.  So it's entirely his credit.  This is not surprising at all.  We are very happy to have him as our quarterback. Proximity. Keep going, Arch.  And I'll take it...Yes. Following.  Darren, you are close with Cal and Anna.  How do they feel about such a start? Well, I'm sure you talk to them more often than I do, but... look, they want to see us win, you know?  They support us, and in the end they just want us to win football matches.  So I appreciate their support.  We sometimes communicate weekly.  Hey, what happened?  What was there? What do you need?  Cal is just wonderful.  He seems to be asking: what do you need?  Having such support and such an attitude from the owners says a lot.  This is very important.  They believe in the work we are to do.  That's all we can ask for—their support.  And that's all we can do: help the organization as much as possible.  I think that's what I've been doing every day since I was hired in '21, and it's not going to stop. With the kind of open door policy you have with him, it seems as if the checkbook is always open too.  Do you feel you have attracted the best players for this organization to succeed? Well, we try to put together the best team that we think makes the most sense and try to take advantage of our opportunities.  So every year things will be a little different.  Um, so, you know, we're going to look at what we're doing, what capabilities we have, what options we have, who's available, and where the resources are going.  So we're trying to be smart and prudent in how decisions, and, you know, we'll continue to do that.    It's still very early.    It usually takes years to evaluate the results of a draft .  At least , most people probably should do that.  But when you look at this year's draft, how do you think these guys are progressing?  If you go through the draft list a little bit, a lot of them are inactive, so we don't know about the progress because we don't see, for example, Marlon Klein in the game because it's probably special teams or something. Thank you. Yes, they are all at different stages.  Um, Killeen probably played the most.  That is, he was on the field during every play. So, you know, it's safe to say that he's made progress. Um, there are things he can improve on.  Um , you know, Kak missed, let's say , training camp or missed the first four games.  So it's like he's at the very beginning of the season.  But he was on the field.  He made several successful plays.  You know, Klein did well. That means we have a lot of people at the tight end position.  So, um, he has a good attitude.  So, you know, he'll get his opportunities at some point.  I'm sure.  Um, you know, I think Killeen is the one who played the most.  The other guys played more narrow roles. You know, Ramsey played a little more in defense .  He played a little bit in the ball-kicking game .  Um, you know, in general, I mean they're all at different stages. I think your assessment is pretty accurate, you know , we'll have a better idea of what level some of these guys will be at in a year or maybe two. So, you know, I'm glad we have these players and eventually, somehow , they'll get their chance.  All they can do is simply make the most of the opportunity presented, whenever it presents itself.  You and Mo made it clear : 2025 is already in the past, it's a different year now, but before the season started you said that the offense would be difficult, the defense would be the foundation, and the offense would have to catch up.  Where does this train of thought come from?  Does that come from what you saw during the offseason training camp program? And if you haven't seen it, why is the solution to stay the course and not change anything? Well, I don't think anyone is saying we're not changing anything, you know.  This applies to both staff and what we do a little differently.  So, I think that this point of view—and I don't want to speak for Demo.  I mean, you can ask him. But he has a strong belief, you know, in the players and a strong belief in the team, and expressed it that we believe in our players and believe that we are capable of, you know, ultimately having a good football team.  At this point, the results are what they are. So we can't change what has already happened.  All we can do is focus on where we are today and stay focused on where we are going next.  Like I said, we're trying to have a good week now and, you know, next week.  We're trying to prepare for, you know, a good Chargers team, who I would say are similar to us in some ways. I mean, they're probably better than their results in the table.  But that's just the reality of how things work out sometimes .  So, I think Demo has a lot of faith and confidence in our players, and he's not afraid to express that, and I, of course, support him in that 100%.  You just mentioned this a second ago season.  You said you considered him your best offensive lineman.  Do you think this has been confirmed over the year?  How are you? Yeah at times we had guys who played a little inconsistently. Some guys from start to finish, I would say, were pretty good .  So, he did some good things. Um, you know, he's probably going through some growing up difficulties.  Um, you know, Braden played, like, 25 snaps yesterday.  It was, you know, without Blake, so it was his first opportunity to play.  So, um, you know, again, I think he's a good player.  I think he will become a good player.  You know, he can definitely do some things better.  He can certainly improve. So, um, yeah, but you know, we're glad he's here, and I think he goes through his ups and downs like most young players and rookies.    The next question was about indecision. Yes.  I mean, there was no indecision, no one hesitated about anything.  So we had discussions, we made a proposal.  Good.  They couldn't quite reach a final decision or agreement.  I mean, this happens.  This is not the first time.  This is not the last time.  So this wo n't be the first time.  So, again , no one is upset.  So, you know, I have a lot of respect for CJ, David and their group.  So, I'm sure that at some point it will sort itself out What made you easily part with a draft pick for Marvin Harrison Jr., a pick that seemed to be quite valuable to you in the past, a second-round pick?  So, ultimately, we felt comfortable doing this deal if it was a player we had the opportunity to work with.  I think part of it was that you have the opportunity to get a player not just for this year and next, but potentially the year after that, depending on what happens this year. So I mean, given the compensation, you're either ready to make that decision or you're not. Ultimately, we felt we were ready to take this step, and you know, we're glad it's here.  So, again, we'll probably have a better idea closer to the second half of the year where we are.  We have a player under contract for next season, that's for sure, and then maybe he'll stay for another year, but that partly depends on, you know, what happens this season.  So, I think you need to consider everything, take into account every factor, and then make a decision—whether you are willing to pay such compensation or not.  And ultimately, we felt like, you know, we were ready to do it, so we made this exchange. Continue. Yes.  I'm listening to you, Kim.  I'll give you...Go on. Used to help the team in a way other than at the wide receiver position. Yeah, I don't think anyone is really worried about the draft right now.  So, there are many ways to turn the peaks at some point, you know, along the way.  So, will it happen this year or, you know, in the offseason.  So, um, again, I don't think anyone is too concerned about the lack of this peak.  If we eventually get that peak at some point, great .  If not, there are other mechanisms that, you know, we can use to supplement the team.  So Sorry, I wanted to clarify my question: Is using this asset to help the team through a trade for another player at a different position possible? Yes, I would say, just assessing the situation based on the information I have. I mean, I'm sure there aren't many players that I would say this draft pick would or could be relevant to.  And again , that's all we can do— act on the information we have. See, when things change, maybe two or three weeks after the exchange, maybe , but that's the reality of how things happen.  So, um, again, I think when we were making the decision at that point, it was more like, "Okay, this is where we are."  Here's an opportunity, okay, we feel confident , great.  If not, um, again, I suspect we probably wouldn't trade a second-round pick on November 11th for another player.  I could be wrong, but I think that was part of the calculations we took into account. Keep going, Kip. Um, a little clarification so I understand Kristi's question correctly about when we ask about last year's team.  I know things change, but there are usually also conversations that build on what has already been started. So I think the confusion, at least for me, is that there's such a big decline in so many of the same people.  Has the league just gotten that much better, or how do you explain it? Yes, look, every year will be different.  Um, to be honest , some of our good or best players probably didn't play as well as they could.  So that's just think there's a better answer than this.  So , again, every year is different.  Team 25 was Team 25. And the 2016 team.  That's where we are with the 2016 team. So I think the focus is on trying to improve, and that applies to all of us. Both individually and collectively, so I think that's what the focus is on .  I know we all try to make predictions sometimes, and that's fair.  We understand that, but it just doesn't match the reality of how things are happening. Every year is different. Every week is different. You all see what happens in the league every week.  It's different every week. That's just the reality of the NFL. I know you were in the front row during his entire journey and everything he did to get back.  What was it like for you to see Tank Bale back on the field yesterday? Yeah, from a personal perspective, it's a pretty cool moment, seeing a player who, frankly , had a near- career-ending injury. Um, having spent as many months as he did. It really speaks to individuality and the person themselves.  So, a pretty cool moment. Of course, the fans felt it in a certain way too.  At the end of the day, there is a human factor, I know it's football and we kind of remove that human factor, but it's there and it was important for him to get recognition and be in that position.  Pretty cool moment.  I'm sure everyone will be quite receptive to this.  And now we'll see if he can keep moving forward.  Okay, that's a good first step .  Well, let's see how the rest of the season goes. So all you can do is hope you stay healthy .  I mean, there's nothing more important than health.  Um, but yeah, it's pretty cool that he went out there and, you know, contributed.  I mean, he made a reception and then he came back on a punt return, which I'm sure made everyone nervous, but, you know, he gained 11-12 yards, which is all we ask for on a punt return to get a first down. So, this is a really great moment for Tenki.  I think you mentioned good negotiations with CJ representatives .  Was there a big difference between your offer and their requests?  Um, and if not, why not try to finish it with them? Yes, listen, I have nothing more to add. So, I mean, we negotiated, discussed different options, didn't reach an agreement, no offense, everyone moved on, and I think everyone is happy with where we are now.  And at some point I expect we will find an understanding .  I'm not sure it's that difficult. Can I ask you a question?  A lot of the players you signed as free agents, Braden, Smith, Teller, Blanket, did n't have a great start.  How can you explain this? Again, Braden was not healthy.  So this is his first opportunity to play. Therefore, let's exclude it from this equation.  I think when we signed Teller, we weren't really sure where we were with the offensive line.  It was an opportunity to get an experienced player who, if not a starter, would probably be a very good backup;  It was a three-on- two situation at guard, and that's how it ended up .  I don't think anyone knew we were going to draft Rutledge right when we did, so these are independent deals.  And then, okay, you put together a team, and ultimately, you field the players in the formation that we think makes the So, Wyatt was great to work with, he has a good attitude;  he had to come out and play at different times.  So, you know, I'm glad he's here.  Um, you know, Reed probably didn't play, you know, he, a lot of people, he said that, I mean, probably in the first round, you know, didn't play very well.  But I would say that in the following weeks, you know, he played good football, played more confidently, more consistently.  You know, he had one of his best matches there.  You know, Jacksonville made a few plays and he got injured. So, um, again, I mean, if you want to look at a quick snapshot of what happens over four or five games, then feel free to do so. So I don't think anyone is upset, and at some point the picture could change by the end of the season, and if they get the opportunity , then, you know, let's see what they can do with it When it comes to scouting, you look for good players who make tackles or those who don't get penalized.    Is there a way to sometimes look and say, you know, we think these players might be more prone to this, and a lot of the problems arise because of that .  Is there anything in their past when you look at guys, at some players who make or miss tackles, because they were sometimes your best players at it, or not?  But what do you think? Yes, I would say that delight is ultimately a matter of psychology.  I can scout as much as you want.  So it's a mentality.  You either want to throw your body at someone, which is what we actually teach—body to body, and, you know, initiate contact.  I mean, part of our problems is that we don't embrace, we don't push, we don't complete the action. Rapture is a state of mind.  So ultimately it's a matter of your mentality and physical stamina, and there's also an element of mental toughness involved .  Um, as for the penalties, I mean, it's just focus and discipline.  I mean, can you search for this somehow? Can you see this ?  Um, again, even some of our make some of these mistakes.  So, you know, you just need to be a little more focused, um, in some of these areas.  And I think it's possible if you can do it.  So, can you look at your question with optimism?  Both yes and no.  But ultimately, it's a attitude.  And I think then you look for the mentality and the mindset of the players to see if they have what it takes.  I mean, honestly, look, guys, some players are tough and some aren't.  I reality.  So, DJ Kim, let me ask you one last question. Yes, you mentioned earlier that the offensive line was inconsistent. It's obvious that since you've been here, you've invested a lot of resources into this unit.  Why do you think you were able to achieve that there were no weaknesses in it , to make it more stable, or at least one that you could rely on to help you win games? Well, I do n't really have a good answer.  I mean, you know, we try to release the guys that we think are the best when they get the opportunity.  Sometimes it's a matter of confrontation , when their player is better than ours. OK.  Is this normal? Can we do something a little differently? So, again, we've done a pretty good job of passing defense this season. Blocking during takeaways is a bit more about completion than anything else.  You know, if changes need to be made , we'll make them, and if not, we'll we can make adjustments elsewhere. Keep going, Kim. When you consider bringing in talent, whether it's free agents, trades, or any other means, do you think about whether they fit your game plan, or do you look at them individually as players, assessing who they are, what they can do, and how they will work with what you have? Yeah, I think we always try to understand: here's the player, here's what he does well, here's his strengths and weaknesses, and then— okay, once this player is here, we know what we're going to ask of him. So, again, you always have to start with the player and just focus on some of the things that they do.  I wouldn't say that players are so dependent on a scheme that they can only play in one specific one.  Many players can play in many different offensive or defensive schemes, and you've seen it yourself all over the league. So, in the end, what matters is what is required of them, and whether they have the qualities, skills, and characteristics that will allow them to succeed.  Getting back to the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. When Higgins was out during training camp , we knew you'd probably make a trade to fill that void, especially considering Tank hasn't returned yet.  But you went for it, got Ken Booty, and now you have Tank coming back, and Higgins coming back next year.  When you made that deal, to what extent did you take into account that the squad was full and that you had many players whose contracts were expiring soon?  Will you continue them?  Will you let them go?  I players like Tank.  You players like Hutch.  This group of receivers is very crowded and very talented.  How did you evaluate it?  And my next question is: now that we know the problem, with two wins and five losses, what is the solution? I'll start with the second question.  The solution is that we again need to play more consistently and if we can improve some of the aspects that have been talked about, we can see a better result. question, I think we saw an opportunity to get a good player, and our job is to get as many good players as possible, and then we'll figure it out.  So it's not necessary to get too hung up on contract situations, understanding that everything can change .  You may think things are going one way , and then the offseason comes and you find yourself in a different situation.  You know, it's not like a game of " duck-duck-goose." Like, we'll do this because this is what's going to happen .  This is difficult to say.  It's hard to define it because the free agent market is kind of a separate story. You think you're going to lose a player.  And then you can hold him, you know, we just think, "Hey, here's a player."  Here is the opportunity right in front of us.  Does this make sense?  OK. Demo and I have been talking about this for weeks.  And finally, we said, " Okay, here's the situation."  Here is the compensation associated with this .  Are we satisfied with this? Okay, great.  And let's make a decision.  So, I would say that's what influenced the choice. Thank you.  Thank you.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: ready. >> Yeah. >> So, congratulations on yesterday. >> I know you say it's about the players, which I'm sure your your players love, but are you able to share beyond what happened in the locker room that the Dolphins Twitter account posted? Can you share with us anything else that neat that happened personally for you in the hours that followed? Like did Wanstead send you a text? Something along those lines that that that was neat and meaningful to you? >> Yeah, I mean Dave, yeah, called me. Um, you know, the cool part was, right, the locker room was really it kind of caught me off guard, right? I usually greet all the players, win or lose, outside the locker room. When I walked in, I didn't expect to have a waterfall on me. Um, but I appreciated that. I mean, that was special. I could I could sense just as I was excited for the players, I felt like the players were excited for the coaches and myself and I think that says a lot about the team that we have and um that meant a lot to me. Like truthfully, it kind of caught me off guard. And then after the game when I walked out when I finished up with the media, my mom, my brother, and my sister were right outside the door. So that was, you know, more meaningful than any text or or um you know, other than my wife. She'd kill me if I didn't include that. Um, but that was really meaningful to me to see my mom, my brother, and my sister, you know, growing up there and and going to games there. I I think it was special for all of them. So, um, it [clears throat] was a good day. Thanks for asking, Mary. >> There's a fraction of this fan base that this season with any win would actually worry about the potential negative impact on a draft pick. Being with this group and seeing it come together, what would you tell anyone who picks that way? >> Yeah. Um, I have a hard time even kind of grasping that to be honest with you. I mean, I think everything we do and and every mo move we make and every day we give everything we got to try to go win a game. So, um I hope they see that and I hope they're happy that we won the game and and hopefully we'll get more. Um but we're going to keep working and that's our goal and um you know I I can't even like grasp that in my head. >> One and0 after the buy. >> One and0 after the buy. Yes. How does this win fuels the team for the next one against the Patriots and the rest of the season? >> Yeah. Um, obviously you could, you know, you could feel the energy and the excitement. It's what I thought. There's a lot of young guys. A lot of this team has never won an NFL game. So, a lot of it today it's their first Monday. I mean, I didn't even have to give a victory Monday because most of the players on our team don't even know what a victory Monday is. They're too young. Um, but you could see that you could see the energy and the excitement and the confidence. Um, and at the same time, you know, when I watch the tape with them, it's win or lose. I mean, we got to be real with each other and turn on the tape. And when you watch the tape, it's always nice to put the result aside, win or lose, and just focus on what we did well, what we need to do better, and move on. But but but you can sense the the energy in the building. Um, but but to talk about, you know, when we took the break, you know, erasing the five games, getting to this 12game season, starting in 1 and 0, really hitting hard on the division, right? in the importance of a division game on the road, which is hard to do, and get a division win. Um, the guys the guys were happy last night and there's there's good energy in the building, but I think there's though it's a young group, it's a mature group and they understand that, you know, after they leave the building today, it's over and and we have a really good team coming in the coming to play us at home. So, we we've got work to do and we got to get back to it. >> But, I like your energy >> with the decision to go for it on fourth down. There were a couple of other calls earlier in the game where you decided to go for it uh to win in that fashion um and get the the positive results that you wanted to. How important is that in aligning with how you want this team to be built on physicality, on toughness on on those gutsy type of calls? >> Yeah, I appreciate that because everything everything we keep asking about identity like what's our identity? Who are we? Who do we want this team to build as we build and we build this foundation? Like the things you just talked about are really important to me. It's toughness. It's resiliency, it's physicality, it's how we play the game. So, the two instances of that which I'm just super proud of is, you know, we got hit on a big play and and we strained to get the ball down at like the one yardd line and I showed that clip today and, you know, that could have easily been a touchdown on that play and then it was first and goal on inside [clears throat] the one yard line and they wound up going backwards three plays in a row. I mean, that's our that needs to be our identity, right? when things get hard or are we going to, you know, go in the tank or we going to step up and fight? And I it's like when you're 0 and five, are you going to, you know, you going to go fight or you just going to go back into a corner? It's the same thing being on the goal line on that on that three plays. And and I was proud of that's who we are that that that's who we need to be and then we get in the same same thing at the end of the game. We have a chance to drain out the clock and win the game. Like we ran the same play three times in a row on offense and it was awesome. I mean, we just we ran a gaps game play three times in a row and we got to fourth and one or fourth and whatever it was. And um it we need to be able to finish out games. That's we have to be a tough physical when the game's on the line, you know, we got to be able to close it out. And when I looked into the guy's eyes, I could see it and I could feel it. And after that, there was no way we weren't going to go for it. And and Bobby made the right call and running the sneak. And the push was awesome. And the cool part is when you watch that and I showed the guys the TV copy just in the team meeting. I mean you got a guy in the ground when the when the referee went first down. I was Cas Merrick was on the ground. You could see his energy almost popping off the ground. Proctor I don't even know what he did. He jumped so high in the air and he um he was excited. Brew and and all the guys Jonah and all those guys you could just see the excitement and the enthusiasm. I mean that that's really important to me as we build. >> Congratulations. Thank you. Um, and and you touched on it as you went through the first six weeks and you said the maturity and even though you were losing, the players knew what this was about. There was a process here and I wasn't going to let them get them down, but mentally getting one and sure they're excited today, but do you think that helps? Is there is this you think that gives them a different feeling than all right, we're 0 and six, we're seven, but they have one to show that what they're doing is paying off. >> Yeah, for sure. and and and I meant what I said. I mean, as we're sitting here 0 and five last week, coming in a buy and there's this excitement and this energy and the I mean, really just trusting the process and focusing on the process. I mean, it's real. I mean, but at the same time, I mean, you play the games to win the games, right? So, to get that win and to really, for some guys, it it gives them more confidence. For some guys, it gives them more belief. For some guys, it gives them justification of, you know, I can really trust the process and continue to do so. Um, so I I do think it's important, right? Um, now I think it's important to get back to what we do and move forward, but but certainly I'd be lying if I said no. >> Coach, kind of piggybacking off your answer to Atlanta, I wanted to ask you about the eligibles playing without the football. What can you say about those guys strain and being selfless to help their teammates? >> Yeah, it's inspiring. It's part it's half the time I spend my meeting talking about it's I mean it's easy when you have the ball and you're making plays to go out and strain and guys are getting you know all the praise and all the love but take a guy like Herman you know all he does is block and strain and fight. and he didn't touch the ball one time yesterday and those wide outs some of the blocks that they're making and throwing in like Chris Bell how physical he was and CD yesterday and Malik Washington and um it's like Casmmer I mean he didn't he didn't really touch touch the ball much but but how much do you love your teammates how much you want to win and that it goes back to our our identity right it to me it's who the guys are without the ball in their hand how hard they're playing right it's the same thing with the corners tackling to me and I know that kind of sounds like eh That's just no, that is important because as you keep going and you build, those are the things that are going to eventually pay off down the road. Um, and those are the it's it's like the O line. It's like if you watch Jonah yesterday, I mean Jonah was so physical against what I thought is a really good front. I mean, that old line yesterday, I mean, the way they played, the physicality, watching Brewer run down the field and guys like Jonah and Proc and Pat and Austin. I mean, it was it was fun to watch and I just we got to keep we got to keep highlighting that because that to me is more important than a wide receiver catching a touchdown pass when he's wide open in the end zone. >> I did want to ask you about getting the ball to the tight end because we didn't get to Greg Doulich yesterday after the game. uh the impact going forward that getting the tight end more involved can >> Yeah, I thought Doulich played a really good game. I thought Malik's decisions and decisiveness getting the ball to him quick. He threw hot a few times when in zero pressure when you know they really outnumbered us in the box, but then watching Greg break some tackles and make some plays. I mean, the one he had on the screen, we didn't even block the guy in front of him and he had a huge play down in the red area. And then there was another one, he caught the ball beautifully in zone coverage, drop stepped and got vertical and got about six, seven more yards. I thought he played a really good game and it was good to see. I thought Bobby called a really good game getting him involved. Um, but he had a really good day yesterday. >> Some of that come as a byproduct of tonight have your full receiving core, Caleb Douglas coming back in that draws more attention from the defensive. >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, you get I think it all starts getting the run game going, right? You get the run game going, it opens up your pass game, and then all of a sudden you get the pass game going to some of those guys on the perimeter. And now you got a tight end who might be open as a check down or somewhere in short zone. And and he's got the ability to catch and run. >> What was the difference between coaching and playing with a lead as opposed to with a deficit, especially in the first and fourth quarters. >> Yeah. You know, first time for a lot of our guys, right? And and we hit that pretty hard. I mean, we were up 21-7 and then it was we had a chance. I mean, and this is where we got to learn. We had a chance at 21-7 on offense to go up multiple scores. We we couldn't get it done. We had a chance on defense. We had a third down and long on the minus side of the field and it was 21-7. We had a chance to get off the field there and we didn't execute right. We had a chance to make the play and then all of a sudden, right, it's a different game. Then you get the ball back and now is it a three-possession game because, you [snorts] know, most of these games are going to come down to the last possession of the game and if you can ever get up by those three possessions, it changes a lot. Um, you know, and then the game got tighter. It got to it got to 2114 and then um you know then we fought back and eventually we we hit the big play when it got really close within a field goal. We hit the play down the sideline. We had a chance to get off the field on the two-minut on two-minute drive which was the first time on defense we were in that. Um you know so new situation again for a lot of players that are starting to come up that we practice but it's always different in the game right and I think you know coming out of halftime you you got to go into that it's the first time we had a lead. You got to go into the second half like it's 000 and I think it's a good learning experience for the guys. >> We saw a lot of really good things from Willis. What impressed you the most things? >> Decision making. I thought he got the ball out really quick. I thought he played with confidence and then when the plays weren't there, the ability to, you know, make the plays with his feet, not take a sack. He had a big fourth down conversion. He had the big conversion in the red zone right before the half. I mean, just looking back at that drive, that drive was like 8 minutes and 30 something seconds and we got we were able to take the clock all the way down to six. Um, so just leading the offense in those key moments and then the biggest thing was just protecting the football. I mean, that's what we talked a lot about it this week to to to beat a team, we got to we got to win the turnover battle. And um, he did a really good job of taking care of the football. Coach, going back to that play that sealed the deal, fourth and one to run down the clock. You had the two-minute warning to talk to your offensive lineman and we caught a glimpse of what you said in the locker room, right? That the trust was there. Can you just walk me through that moment and that conversation you had with the whole offense just to make sure you guys were set up for victory information? >> Yeah, I just in that drive I I just it really it it was really the last play. I mean, exactly. I'll tell you exactly what happened. I said, "Hey, Bobby, hang on a second. We had the we had the two-minute warning and um I I told everybody I said, "No, I want to see the O line." So, I called the whole line over and I wanted to look them all in the eye. I said, "Guys, if we get the first down, we're kneeling and we're winning this game. So, I can either punt the ball or we play defense or we're going to go for it." I said, "What do you guys want to do?" And they looked at me and said, "Coach, we're going for it." And I said, "Okay, we better get it." And I walked back. I said, "All right, Bobby, call your call the play." and we talked about the play and we decided to go with the sneak and um and we got it. But I I just think I think anytime you can talk to players and give them ownership, I just the type of guys that we have, I was pretty confident that we would get it out of them. Um and I trust those guys and I think, you know, that will help us as we build. >> There were three possessions that I thought were significant. you've already mentioned to the the goal line stand where they go backwards for three plays, the quarterback sneak, but then the final possession of the first half um you guys score and including Malik sliding and staying inbounds. How significant was that possession and and even what Malik did there that awareness? >> Yeah, and it goes back to the things that he did well. I thought decision-m was huge. Um yeah, it was 21 it was 14 to7 and we had the ball with 8 minutes left. I mean, at any time you can because they're going to get the ball at halftime, right?
