So, usually you can't take eight minutes off the clock, but to be able to run the ball and eat it up and then stay in bounds like we did. We did twice. We did it once on the far sideline and then when Malik scrambled for the first with the thought in mind and keep the clock running and either force them to call a timeout or take another 40 seconds off. I mean, it was huge. Um, you know, again, you look at Malik as a guy that is a first year starter in his first six games and hopefully he continues to grow along those lines. Um, which he did a nice job. >> The, uh, subtle tweaks in the running game stand out to me each week. The offset formation you guys used a bunch yesterday, for instance. I was hoping to get your perspective on that and just the job that Bobb's doing scheming up the run game each week. >> Yeah, it's Bobby, it's Zack, it's it's the offensive staff, you know, and again, I thought Bobby called a really good game yesterday. I thought the offensive staff did a really good job. It's just starting to figure out what we're good at, right? And you can see there's a variety of the run game. There's a lot of gap scheme. There's a lot of outside zone, which which we've run for a long time. Um, and then there's creativity with where are we going to line up the fullback? Where are we going to line up the tight ends? And a lot of it is the same for us, but making it look different for them to cause different adjustments on the defense and different movements and trying to gain leverage. And I think that's always really important when you look at an offensive run game versus a defense. It's all about angles and leverage. And they're doing a really good job of creating good angles and good leverage for us to be able to run the ball and then we're getting the movement. Um but it is it's making it hard to defend >> the two-point conversion uh where Gino completed it to Mason Taylor. Can you kind of take us through what what went wrong there? >> Yeah, the one at the end of the game. Yeah. Um, we were in a call where we were in a call where we basically, for a lack of going into too much detail, we basically had uh we had two guys covering the tight end and whoever didn't take the tight end was going to be responsible for the quarterback. So, we grabbed the tight end with Taff and then Trader was going to go get the quarterback. And it just so happened when Gino started the scramble, Taff didn't see anybody cuz Trader was back a little bit further. So Trader was coming to go and get the quarterback. He was on a different level. So Taft came off his man thinking he had to go get the quarterback to try to make a play, which you don't fault him. The quarterback's about to score and he's just trying to make a last stitch effort to save him. Um so [clears throat] just again two two young players that probably haven't been in that situation where they just got to trust the the one's going to be where the other should. Um but good play by him. How much how much can the defense take out of three plays back from the half yard line to the two to the three or whatever it was back to the 15. Three plays you knocked them back three times and it's with the game on the line they could have tied the score. >> What can that do now moving forward? I >> I think it it it teaches you a huge lesson. Um, you got to defend every blade of grass and that's why you strain and you fight and you just keep playing until it's either a touchdown, a field goal or you get off the field. I mean, it's just it again, it has to be who we are as a team. You just you just keep fighting. Um, you keep playing the next play and they were able to do that. I I do think it's such a huge lesson. Um, and it was really inspiring to see them that drive me a lot. I mean, that's a that's a big deal. >> Coach, a really talented team coming to town. Yeah. Division rival, a little bit more rested to play Thursday night. You've talked a lot about, you know, playing your game, controlling what you can control. Um, what do you need to see from your guys this week leading up to a game against the Patriots? >> Again, um there's plenty from that game that we have to improve and we'll make a big deal of that. It's got to continue to be about ourselves. um we are playing a really good team and one of the best teams in the NFL and um clearly last year what they were able to do. So, you know, we'll we'll we'll get them rested today. We'll get them back Wednesday and and we got to have great practices. We got to know our opponent. We got to study them really well. Um, but we we have to continue to get better. And I think this whole year you're going to get bored of me saying that, but it's got to be about us and developing these players because I think what you're seeing is we are these young guys are starting to play better and there is development and that's got to continue to be the main thing. It's growth and development. So when you turn on the film week 17, are we better than we are right now? Because the whole key, it's kind of like I joked with you guys about Chop like you got to do it again, right? Malik had a good game. All right, let's let's go do it again. It's got to be a whole our whole team. So, we'll keep it about us. Um, but I'm excited to get back to work. I know they'll take some time off. We'll start game planning tonight and I can't wait for practice. I've loved being around these guys. I've loved coaching these guys and and we'll keep fighting. Thanks, guys.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (10/26) | Week 8 | New York Jets
text: with an opening statement. >> All right, good morning. When it comes to injuries, um I'll have a better update for you guys uh later in the week. Again, Sweat was the only one that was in the game with the knee injury and um I have more information about that um again later on in the week. When it comes to the game, obviously disappointed in the outcome of the game. Um there's some things that I did think we did a better job. I thought the offense did a better job of of moving the ball and and scoring. Um we didn't have those opportunities. Uh defensively, um wasn't really happy on the way that we started the game. come back in the second half. We made some adjustments and I thought we played a lot better in the second half. What we have to do as a team is just bottle that up what we did in the second half and be able to do that for a whole game and be able to win in the margins and those are some things that I feel like we have to do a better job of. Obviously, we got the um a one yardd line and we did a good chance to get a score and kicking the field goal in that situation and those situations that we have to score and take advantage of those situations. But this whole week, um, and I said this yesterday, uh, Sunday can't get here fast enough for us. Um, this whole week is going to be about improving in those things and making sure that, um, there's a focus on just making sure that everything that we do is towards us improving. So, um, in saying that, uh, any questions? Aaron, I know you addressed the uh the timeout thing at the end of the first half uh yesterday after the game, but I'm just curious in terms of the process there. >> Yeah. >> Do you do you have John Burger in your ear? Do you have Frank in your ear? What goes on there? Are you ultimately the person that's deciding not to call timeout there? And do and also do you guys have is Frank on on on the headset saying, "Hey, I think we need to we need to get a possession here at the end here. Let's call these guys out." How does that work there? >> Yeah. So, I I've talked about that at length on how we actually go about these things. And I want everybody to know that there's a process on how we go about u making those decisions and um each week uh starting on Tuesday. All right. We um me, Burger, and Arjun, we we talk through those things. I think you guys are well aware of that. And as we get in the end of the week, we talk more about them. But there's a process and a strategy that we go by. Um, and I want to make sure we keep that strategy to ourselves. And the thing is, at the end of the day, we got to do a better job and I have to do a better job. And I said that yesterday. And to me, I think that's the most important part of making sure we just try to improve in those uh in those areas. >> I guess strategically speaking though, why would you not want to get another possession at the end of that half when it's clear you could have manufactured one with some timeouts there? >> Yeah, there was a lot of things that go into that. I think they had the ball to 30 um with uh with the three timeouts left and um also thinking they have time to get more first downs to negate the timeouts that we have. So we call timeout. All right. Then we're using those and as we use all of then they get another first down right then they can run the clock out. So there's things that um that we strategize when it comes to that of using those. But again um I have to get better in those situations. And on the uh just to jump on that two-minute situation again, more of a broader view, you guys have been outscored like 107 to6 in the last two minutes of the first half. >> Yep. >> Over over one and a half years. >> Um how how troublesome is that to you and why can't that why doesn't that get fixed? >> Well, the thing is we're trying. We're trying. Um the thing that we do on Wednesday is we do a twominut um jog through on Wednesday and then we come back and we have a live twominut on Thursday and then we have another two-minute on Saturday. So it's not like that that we're not trying to get that done. We just got to improve in our execution. Uh I have to improve on on in both sides on how we manufacture these things. So um I mean it's a process of getting these things done. I know it's um it's frustrating, you know, for for for for the fans. I know it's frustrating for the players. It's frustrating for us as coaches, but we just got to continue to work at it. And as long as we continue to do that, I I just know that we'll get better at it. >> Erin, on the goal line, you had the ball at the one yard line there. Uh giving the ball to Beck seems like an odd choice. I don't mean to be disrespectful to Beck, but you know, he only had one carry last year. He had no carry so far this year. Could you just walk us through, you know, the decision that you I assuming you discussed that with Frank to to hand the ball to back there rather than going Braylin or somebody else who might get the ball more. >> To me, when you look at that, it it doesn't matter who gets the ball. We have to score at the one yard line, you know? I think it really just comes down to that. So, I don't want to put it in a situation of give to Brilen, give to Beck. It's we just have to score and we have to get better there. So, um to me, that's how I look at it. Erin, have you spoken to either Garrett or Frank? We know that Garrett was frustrated yesterday. We saw it on the sideline. Have you spoken to either of them? And and I'm just curious that like it seems weird that you have to remind you have to get in Frank's ear to tell him to get Garrett the ball. I mean, top receivers are always getting the ball throughout the league. >> Yeah. Here's um and yes, I I I've spoken to Garrett and and we sp we'll speak to him again and yes, me and Frank always talk about it, but you take a look at at that situation and obviously at this game um they were trying to make sure they take Garrett out, but to be honest, like that wasn't the issue when it comes to offense. I thought we moved the ball. I thought we scored points. Um but we know for a fact that every game, man, Garrett is our top priority to make sure we get the ball. But make no mistake about it, I think offensively we did some good things as far as man and when they were doubling Garrett, man, who was open. And I think that's the essence of what you have to do is make sure that when you have an opportunity to throw to an open receiver, man, you take that opportunity instead of forcing the ball. Um, but as much as possible, and I think you guys know this, we're trying to get the ball to Garrett as much as we can. How do you how do you feel about a player getting that emotional and animated on the sideline seemingly directing it at one of your assistant coaches on the bench? >> Well, I think sometimes that's that's um that's that's overblown as far as what people think is happening. Sometimes that can be those those conversations be totally something else. And listen, I I I know for a fact that Gino Garrett, it was more or less, man, let's get going. let's let's let's let's get the offense going more than guys bickering at each other. So, I think sometimes that get overblown. Um, and I know what type of player Garrett is. I know what type of player Gino is. And I know where their hearts at, too. And I know for a fact that that was more or less, man, let's get the offense going and try to score points. >> Hey, Jarvis. Jarvis Brownley was a healthy scratch. Can can you uh explain that decision? >> Yeah, I'm going to keep that in house between um between me and and Jarvis. Um, and we'll go from there. >> AJ, was that was that >> was that a disciplinary decision? >> I just answered that. We're going to keep that in the house. >> Ag, you you kind of referenced this at the top yesterday uh in your postgame comments, but it's going to get noisy this week around your team, around you. >> How do you uh what's your message to your team in terms of trying to uh not splinter this week? Well, that's basically it that we know it's going to get noisy and I mean that's just what happens um in this league, you know, with any team, especially at this point when the record is not exactly where it needs to be. Um the most important thing for us and I think our guys would do a heck of a job with this is just man blocking out everything on the outside. Just focus on like who we have in this building and then just improving, you know, and it all starts with how we go about practice. It all start with how we go about meetings. It all starts with how we go about in walkthroughs and that's where the the the focal point would be for us. Um we get it. We understand that this league is about winning and we have to do a better job when it comes to that and um and I promise you man, we're focused on that and we're trying to do everything we can to to to get those wins and that's what we look forward to each week. >> I know I know you addressed um his tackle on the long touchdown there. Just when you went back and watched Phil, what did what did you think of his performance yesterday? And I guess what have you thought of his contributions to the team so far this year? >> Say that again. Who you who you who you talking about >> with Minka? >> Yep. And >> you talk you mentioned you I know you referenced the uh yeah the long touchdown yesterday. But when you watched his whole game, what did you think of his performance and and what have you thought of his contributions so far this season? >> Yeah. Yeah. I thought Minka did a really good job and obviously throughout the season I think he's doing a good job. that was a situation where he missed the tackle and listen I hold Mink in high regard and he understand himself that he should have made that tackle and again when it comes to plays like that I look at that as a shared process between myself as the play caller and then the players as the execution part of it so um the play call got to be better for the players and then the players got to execute better and to me that's how I look at it so it's it's it's between all of us but to say that I thought Mink has been been doing a good job for us this Thanks everyone. Thank you coach. >> All right. Thank you.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I'm Proud Of Our Style Of Play" | Seattle Seahawks
text: All right. Good to see everybody. Back at it today and then uh guys will be off tomorrow and we'll use our we'll use our extra day on uh on Wednesday. And then uh Thursday will be Wednesday. >> So, what happens Wednesday? >> Uh we're working through like the final details, but it'll be more of a recovery day, more football, won't be on the field. But our guys will be in in some capacity. >> Coach, >> the in the last like 30 years, the Seahawks haven't had a four-game stretch that was as negative offensively as previous four games that then turned into as positive as the one you So, this is only the second time in the last 30 years that's happened. What >> were playing bad and then they played good? >> Yeah, it was actually the Beast Quake game. >> Okay. >> So, like it's not easy to turn around an offense that's not doing that well. Like, what what do you think was the the key factor for you guys in being able to get get things squared away? >> I I just think um I think you just have to look at it through the lens of we're on a this year's this team's version of our journey. And so, you know, what are what are we doing to find solutions to where we want to go. Um I thought we've done some really good things at the first, you know, quarter of the season. Uh I'd say the takeaways leave something to be desired, but I think also like the function, hey, you're going from a Sunday night to a Thursday night. It's a quick turnaround. Didn't necessarily get the returns we wanted. Didn't necessarily have the ample opportunity to really dive in. And so, trying to make the best of the extra time. Um It's also like look, we're we're trying to I mean, it we're doing the same thing on defense. Maybe not to the same degree because we have such familiarity with our staff and our players, but you're always you're always honing in on what you do, how you do it uh throughout the year on really, you know, what your team's going to calling card and identity is going to be. And so, I think that's the process we're going through. >> You Excuse me. Go ahead. >> There were a lot of impressive numbers though on offense. What are the one or two that you want to see just kind of continue to to carry on in the coming weeks? >> Uh I think I'm I'm pro- I'm proud of our style of play. Um watching watching us just play the game felt like our looked like us. And uh there's some things operationally that we're still chasing that got us behind the sticks. Uh red zone, you know, we weren't able to finish those drives off, which that's going to be a that's definitely a point of emphasis, but I think where we focused our attention, that's what came to life. Operation style of play, run game, third down. Um I don't know this you know what I mean? I'm not a big stat guy. I just I'm going off of what we saw on tape. And um you know, that was a felt like felt more our style of ball. >> What what stood out to you most about the defensive effort when you went back and looked at it? >> I I think the same thing. Like I think in order to in order to the we felt like you know at our best we're a wave of defense. There's going to be mistakes. That's that's football. Like it's never going to be perfect, but um how we play on a you know, on like talking about playing off one another, having each other's back, 12 as one. I thought that was that was impressive, man. The guys guys played extremely hard. >> Lately, Mike when your team's had extra time with the bye week, the mini bye, you've performed really well. The team's performed really well. What have you learned in maybe the 3 years as a head coach how to utilize extra days? Like you have one extra day this week. What What do you guys focus most on? >> Funny you say that. Immediately thought of the Tampa game last year. I think that was coming off a Thursday game. >> Since then? >> Thanks. it It takes X amount of time to get ready for a game. So, how you allocate the rest of the time is important. But, like when we've when we've over when we've over done it, we've probably gotten mentally taxed. And the And the week is um drained. And that I was That's really just the solution for us. So, that's That's kind of the philosophy that we've been going off of. So, is it off of cell scout? Is it for recovery? Is it skill development? Uh do we need to get away from each other? You know, I just try to make the best decision for our team on how to use that time the best. >> Do you insulate the players from the extra time prep that maybe coaches are doing and then present them a normal week after that? Or do you involve them in the extra day work stuff? >> it it I think it changes based on the like the what what season of the season you're in. Um normally normally that is kind of the rule of thumb is like I said it's We've learned that, you know, if we have a great {quote} Wednesday, great {quote} Thursday, Friday, Saturday, um we can put a great plan together and play great football. Sometimes it takes more than that, but uh felt like we've fallen short more often than not if we've tried to over overdo it. >> What do you make of Nick Chubb? I mean, where are you Can you talk about his maturation off the field? I mean, you've talked about what We can see what he's doing on the field. What I mean by that is as a young man, as a professional, what are you seeing in terms of his growth? >> Well, I think Nick's been remarkably consistent with with his with his approach. what we're asking him to do and how and how how we're asking him to go about his business is um a little bit different, you know, he's kind of you know, CP's kind of his point of contact, but he's also bounced around with position groups and things like that. And so, amount of time and investment it takes to to do that and also you know, you're not going to be right all the time. You know, so to be able to take the coaching and um stay kind of steadfast in what we're asking him to do is and determine where like, you know, you can get frustrated. Like there's a lot of things going on. There's a lot of things we're asking him to do, but kind of work through that process every week without getting frustrated, I think it's been pretty impressive. >> Is all motivation so important as opposed to intrinsic as opposed to extrinsic motivation for >> Well, I think it's about us, right? You know, everyone again, everybody says that's cliche. It's a cliche. About us. Well, you know, we actually try to make it about us. Sometimes we make it about the other team and a lot of times, you know, after we do that we um feel like we miss we missed the target. >> Is Nick spending more time in the like outside linebacker meeting rooms that the you said Chris Partridge is his point of contact. Is he spending more time >> Yeah, no, he spends majority of time in the DB room and then um kind of all the extra time is with CP or um Shoot, sometimes he's been in Zach's room. He's kind of just bouncing around. >> Because he's so physically gifted, maybe people overlook that side of the work. I mean, what what about him allows him to be, you know, you know, in at multiple position groups, having to learn different roles and then put it out there on Sunday? >> Well, I think there's again, there's a responsibility that comes with that. I mean, if we're if you're going to can't just willy-nilly do like multiple things. You got to for us to be responsible and for us to for us to want to do that as a coaching staff and feel like the team is in a better position for have for having to ask him to do multiple things. Um we feel like the execution has to be a certain level. So, uh there's a responsibility that goes with that and a lot of times it's extra time. It's always extra time, frankly. So, um but we've expected that and and to Nick's credit, uh he wants to do it. You know, he wants to he wants to invest in in his career in which you got no chance you got no choice but to tip your cap to him. >> What what's the latest on Charles Cross? >> Yeah, Charles has an ankle and um we'll see how long it's going to be. >> Okay. You looking at IR at all? >> Uh that's not we haven't had that conversation yet. >> Is it a high ankle sprain? >> Uh it's it's a it's an ankle right now. >> Yeah. >> There was a report he might miss a couple games. >> Yeah, I saw that report. Didn't come That didn't come from me or our trainer, so. >> How about Rasheed Shaheed? >> Uh no no update on Rasheed from this morning. Again, it early returns positive. How long that means, not sure. >> Are you proceeding as if Cross wasn't Is he going to play Monday night? >> Uh I don't We're really not like we're proceeding with anything right now. It's just Monday and we're he's got an ankle and we're going to take it day by day from there. >> This is the third year in a row you've had a new OC to work with and being a defensive coach, it might not be the last time you're breaking in a new OC. >> Yep. >> Have you learned anything uh from that experience about that you might want to take to how to speed it up uh in the future? Yeah. >> Anything you can >> Learn every Learn every day. I mean I I think it's a it's a partnership, right? It's so like any other partnership we have in our building between, you know, John and I working together Jay and I working with our AD. And it it just takes just takes communication, you know, it's like >> What is the the regular season do to help kind of focus that development that maybe you can't get till the regular season starts? >> Um I think it's tough to gauge your effectiveness in certain situations in the off season. You You see what you're doing, you can feel the the spirit of the team, you can feel who's who's performing at a high level. But it just it doesn't um I you know, it's hard it's hard to simulate what the situations are how those play out, you know? And that's where you end up being targeted and how you want to improve based on results and like what goes on in games and how it comes to life. You know, I mean, in the off-season you're installing dang near every day um in some capacity. but it's not like a target you're not game but you're not game planning. And so you're not going through that process of saying, "Hey, we're only going to get x amount of swings today." You know, what do we want that process to look like? How do we want to get there? Who's going here? You're really just trying to expose the guys to the like the things they need to be able to do to perform and then um to try to create that menu so then you can whittle it down once it comes game time. >> Yeah, Mike last night you acknowledged like with losing three or four before this there's more noise around than guys have heard in a while. And how that wasn't a factor for them. Like what is it about this group that kept that from from being an issue? >> Well, I think that's the result of the investment they made into one another. We put up we we invest a lot in like the 12 is one and the connection of the team tough connected mob tight. I mean, all all the all the words you hear. But those aren't just like words that are just in thin air. It's just that's how we've we've chosen to really try to make, you know, create our way of life around here. And you know, we fall short sometimes and it's never perfect, but it's uh I think it's an honest process of what we're trying to create and I think the guys feel that and um it's not going to be the last time that we're in a we're in a we're in a tough spot, you know? It's going to happen plenty and uh it's how we kind of circle the wagons and stick together and you know, keep moving forward that's going to help us get out of those things. >> Mike, just about >> points of emphasis. So, you mentioned earlier it's red zone for the offense, but previously it's been penalties or it's been, you know, attacking at point of contact. How do you maintain multiple points of emphasis, or do you just trust that it gets taken care of once and you don't have to address it again? >> Um It's a good question. You know, it's never like, "Hey, let's get better at this. All right, see you guys tomorrow." You know, that's always Hey, what's our what's our plan? Do we First of all, do we like what we're doing? In terms of the inputs. If yes, let's let's focus on executing better. How can we tweak it? If And then you say, "Oh, well, there's you know, there's some things on defense." We were just having a conversation with like on how we're doing some of our walk-throughs and what we're exposing our guys throughout the week that like that we're going to tweak, you know, it's like like I said, it's like my dad's golf swing, you know, you got to keep tweaking it and until it's uh until you start, you know, hitting the ball in the fairway. >> Mike, with with with Tyree's Knight, uh it seems like just about every time he plays for you, he plays at a really high level. Obviously, you've chosen to go with Drake as a starter for your your reasons, but what has it been like for you guys to have conversations with him, keep him in it when when he's been in the reserve role, and then to see him step into these roles and shine the way he has when he's gotten the opportunity to do so? >> Uh I I I think it's I don't think it's a special conversations. I think um Tyree's knows it. what his role is. It'd be It'd be great if you could start more than 11 guys. But, I think we have multiple players on our defense that deserve to play more. But, uh it's a great problem to have, you know. But, T-Knight know like look, if you're not if you're not playing right now, you're a play away from being a starter. if that's the way he prepares, Zach does a great job with him. The guys love him. Um he's been in there and he's been really productive. And you know, from from my perspective, I you know, okay, T-Knight's playing. Okay, I expect high-level play from our from our from our linebacker core, no matter who's playing. Just And cuz he's earned those expectations, you know? So. Keep it rolling. >> How did you uh assess the offensive line play on second watch? >> Uh guys did a really great job. They did. Um I I I felt those running off the ball. I felt those taking the line of scrimmage. Um I guess I felt the guys trying to finish blocks. I think there are some really great stuff in pass protection. Uh they gave us some tough pressures to be able to pick up and some of them are on like some of them there's going to you're going to have a a rusher that you can't account for and they've been able to handle those looks. So um I think George Iloka did a great job too on third down pass protection. But uh the guys deserve a shout-out. They played really well. >> Uh Ifeatu Melifonwu is um I don't think we asked you about him after the game. >> Yeah, he's he has a hamstring. We're not sure of the severity. So we'll we'll see with Ifeatu. >> Do you Do you know Ben Johnson at all? Have you gotten to know him at all too? Yeah. >> Uh no. I've met him at owners meetings and uh I think that's the only time we've ever met. >> A few weeks ago you said that Byron Murphy was playing some dominant football. I'm curious just what kind of impact that has trickled down on the rest of the defense when he's playing at >> Yeah, it starts with him. You know, you get moved in the A gap, you can do a lot of things behind it, but it's not going to be very effective. So it it starts with Murph. And I think I think the cool thing is like the guys know it too. Like they know that uh they could see how how well he's playing. You know, I I hope I hope everybody else sees it as well. And I and I think you know, he's winning a lot of rushes. I don't I don't know what his sack production is right now, but um he's earned the right to be out there and done a great job. He's done a great job. He's affected the quarterback. He's won a one-on-ones. Um he's played off of guys, so Murph's playing at a really high level still. >> Uh big picture with Shaheed. What have you felt like the way you guys have used him this season on offense so far and what you've got out of that? >> Um I think I think there's there's more there. It's for a lack of effort or a lack of trying or not doing or you know, it's just I think we're just I think that's part of our process of keeping the ball distributed and and finding better ways to get him the ball. You know, that's might be more in his sweet spot, but Saw yesterday like in the return game, it's right there, you know, like our our our our kickoff return and and punt return units are are playing some really good football and giving them some opportunities to really make a difference in the game as well. So, I think uh you know, plan is for us all to continually improve or continually expand, but uh I think there I think there's more >> He was on the interception that he got nicked up. Was that where >> sure what the exact play was cuz to my understanding he came back after it. After he I could be wrong on this, but I think he came back into the game. I'm not I'm not sure. >> You mentioned that Zadarius Smith will practice this week. That's the expectation. Zack started practicing. It was multiple weeks. He still doesn't play. Do you Do you think that that's going to be similar with Price or is there a chance he could play in this game? >> Yeah, this situation's a little different in term obviously for the length of the injuries. Could both play? Yes. Could either play? Yes. Uh Could either one play? Yes. >> How does that work when you've got coaches involved, front office, agents, medical staff? Like how do those conversations work? >> Yeah, they're all they're all different. Uh I just I look at it, what's the best for the player and the team. And when those marry up like we're rolling. When they don't, then you then you want to work work through things, you know. So, it's like it's kind of like the question I had earlier. It's like what what works, you know, communication, figuring it out and then going from there. So, >> What Um ultimately is the last benchmark I guess that you need to see from Zach to know that he's ready to play, we can we can do this? I think I'm going to pass on that answer. >> Going back to Nick, last season you talked about not giving him too much to overwhelm him. Do you feel like you found more of a balance this year in the things that you're giving him? >> said with Nick? >> I think um I think it's just a I think it's a process and also I think you got to let the game plan speak to you. Um we as a as a coaching staff, starting with me and how on how we deploy our people, I think we can be a little bit clearer. And so I can I can do a better job of um helping him out and helping really the rest like it's it's really it's frank frankly it's not it's not just Nick, it's the position group that he's affecting by where we're moving him based on the play. So um so I I can I can help out there and make him even more effective. >> With the way that you use him, is it ever a challenge like with everything that he can do to say, man he would be really great in this role like covering this guy in this play where he'd be really great rushing, is it >> Yeah, for sure. You can you can bet on who lobbies for what based off of what position they coach. >> Anything else? >> Why is it always your dad's golf swing and not yours? >> I got a great swing.

title: Saquon Barkley & More on Loss to Dallas Cowboys
text: Yeah. And it sucks when that's like when you know it's not going the way you want it to go. But I don't know. I just it's kind of like the school thought I come from. Um I I truly love this game and I feel like if you you're able to go sometimes you got to push your your body to the limit. Um and I'm trying. It's just not responding the way I wanted to respond right now. And it sucks cuz trying to be the best leader I want to be and it's hard when you're when you're not able to be out there and perform and for your team, but I I can't make any excuses. Uh that's just the you know the hand I'm dealt with this year right now. And I just got to continue to trust in the trainers and and our strength coaches and everybody which they've been doing an amazing job. the fact I was even to be able to go out there, you know, two weeks after this this hamstring. Um, I wouldn't, you know, they did a really, they did a great job roam and I'm not a easy person to deal with when I'm hurt. Um, so the rehab process and the, you know, the mental the mental part of it. Um, I appreciate them, but it's got to keep going and, you know, it sucks. Just got to keep fighting. If you ran well when you when you were carrying the ball despite the injury, um are you able to kind of just forget about it like during the play and then after the play realize how it hurts again? >> Um your back ever locked up on you? It's like that's the only way I can like kind of explain you your body overcompensate. I'm not trying to get too much into the the injury, but your body that's how the body protects itself a little bit, I guess you can say. And you know, obviously something's a little banged up. So something's got to work a little harder and you have moments where you're able to, you know, relax it, loosen it up, and the position that I play and the thing that I do for a living, you know, you kind of get hit and compress on it a little bit. So just got to do a good job of uh managing that. I thought I thought I did a good job of, you know, firing everything up. Um, I actually got to do a better job of that. How tough is it wrestling with kind of in the mind you see Devonte coming back you know gets injured again with his hamstring and and fighting through compared to as you said being safe with everything and smart about everything. >> Yeah. I mean every injury is its own injury. Um for me it's just unfamiliar territory. I've never really done anything like to my hamstring. I've had like little small strains. You guys seen like my ad there. All my other injuries been like football like someone tackling me or I told my ACL. So, um, you know, felt good at times, but just wasn't good enough. >> Would you probably not have gone if not for the importance of this particular game? >> Um, no, I would have gone. >> You had uh you were on the field for nine plays and you had nine touches. Was this kind of the the plan going in? um you know to have a limited limited snap count but maximize those those reps. What was the what was the plan coming in for you? >> Yeah, I I think we had a great game plan. Um I don't think we had you know I think the back was a little unpredictable a little bit that was supposed to happen. Um I'm just thankful that they allowed me to go. Um they did a really good job the whole week of preparing me. I knew what the game plan was and you know I told my family and everything I was going to be smart and just listen to my body. Um the hamstring came out came out great. The the back just locked up on me. So uh but with that being said, I think Elijah and DP did a great job. They went in there. Um you know, the whole week knowing that I was going to be a little limited um you know, they kept telling me that they had my back and I think Elijah made a big play. Um DP ran ran hard. Uh we just came up short, but um just got to keep going to work. I saw you going up and down the sideline just trying [clears throat] to keep guys motivated and keep going up and down and trying to keep them going in the game. How much, you know, as one of the leaders on this team, how much is that the message going forward and how do you keep these guys from from getting down? >> Um, yeah, kind of the message I had after the game. Uh, I'm not really a big talker to be honest. Um, you know, feel like the moment was right, but it's I I I don't know. Like I I just how I look at life. I feel like you you just never quit. You never get up, give up. You just keep fighting no matter what. Whatever the situation is, how it looked. Um, and you know, I feel like that we have the men in the locker room to do it. We put ourselves in a situation now. We got to dig oursel out of it. And um you know I I know that I got to take more of a you know a role of being vocal you know using my voice. I'm more of a lead by example type of guy. But you know it happens when you when you have guys banged up and you know guy like Jaylen who's really basically the vocal leader. It's going to take you know me and Jordan all all of us kind of fill that void. Um, I think we're doing a great job leading and we're working our ass off and it just it sucks when you know the results aren't going the way you you want it to go. But I'm gonna sound like a broken record, but I really I I bought into this mindset. It just got to keep believing in the process and keep working and keep going. And the results may not be what it wants right now, but um that doesn't matter. You just got to you got to keep going back to work and it's going to take all of us. >> Sorry if you were asked this already. Um, how frustrating is it for you when you're giving the effort that you're that you gave to play and [clears throat] the back kept locking up and the issues kept happening? How how frustrating is that on on the sideline as a competitor? >> Um, super frustrating. Um, outside of loss, that's the thing that's probably the most frustrating. Uh, you know, you see it in your mind one way, you know, um, just didn't go that it didn't go the way I would like it. Um, but rehab and get back and the beauty of this game and this business that we in you can't really harp on a win or a loss too long cuz in those six days we got to go down to commanders and and try to get this thing back on track. So, >> you say you're not much of a voice a vocal leader. Did you feel the need to address the team post game in the locker room? >> Um, yeah. I don't I mean I don't really want to get too much like make it seem like oh I was a guy who like brought the team up but I just there's you know the season and games calls for different moments and you know we all got to our roles change a little bit especially with his ways going. No, not necessarily. Um, you know, this right now we're, you know, lo with these games that we've been losing. Uh, it hurts, but at the end of day, you can't you can't stay on it. What what did you kind of see as as a big issue for them to have as much success as they did? >> Yeah, we I mean I don't think we really helped ourselves. Um you know, started with first down. Ter gave me a great ball. Like I said, the receivers did their job, so you know, I get in the box. How do you maintain possession and roll out of that for the touchdown? >> Um, just the work you put in throughout the week, you know, in the weight room. Um, you know, many reps at that. So, um, so once you in the game, you know, you just you flowing. >> Mai, as a young player, the balance of this team on a fivegame losing streak, but you yourself, you see you progressing every week. Um, you got a job to do, so that's what I'm doing. >> Is it a unique experience for you though to go through something like this? I'm sure you've probably won every level you've been at, right? >> Um, not necessarily. Um, but I definitely say it is definitely unique, but um, you know, you just got to roll with the punches though. You know, just try to be better each week. Um, don't stop and just keep going. Um, like you know, probably her sake on um, you know, just sticking as a family and keep going. >> What have you learned about the NFL through this losing streak? Any lessons to take away? >> Um, you know, the margin of error is definitely, you know, very slim. So, >> um, I'll say that. Here.

title: Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 8 vs Cleveland Browns) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Heat. Heat. Heat. [music] down. >> [music] >> Hey, hey, hey. Heat. >> Good afternoon everyone and welcome to the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. I'm Bob Pompi and this is the Mike McCarthy press conference brought to you by PNC and Mike McCarthy back from France is already at the podium. Let's join him there >> back through training camp. So, but yes, it's a it's a long year. uh you know got a big game coming up with Cleveland in division games. So you know all all those things are you know part of your equation each and every week. But uh you know we definitely want to we want to be running the ball you know with those guys touching the ball is is what it's supposed to look like um as far as the offense and I so I felt really good about their distribution yesterday. Mike, when you were putting together that game plan, what did you see that made you think the jumbo package would be something that would be useful for you? And did this team success with that last year play any part into that decision? >> Oh, absolutely. I I go back to, you know, when you you get the job, the first thing you do, you sit down, you start going through the personnel and, you know, [snorts] Spencer, um, I was so impressed uh, with him and it was a big part of, you know, the discussion of how we were trying to forecast him uh, for where we felt he could play because I mean, he played so many positions. You know, I did a similar experience with Connor McGovern. you know, he's um up here in Buffalo now. And the whole time we were together in Dallas, it's like, hey, we we got to get him on the field. He's, you know, is he a guard, is he a center, he can play fullback, he can, you know, he can do all those things. So, when you have someone like Spencer with his unique talents, uh it gives you such great versatility, but in fairness to him, you know, I want to give him a chance to compete for a job. So, and that's why we started the way we did and, you know, and with him at the right guard and then, you know, he had the injury and so forth. So, uh, he he carries a lot of value on on our football team, you know, especially up front and, uh, and it's important for us to continue to, you know, create opportunities for him. >> You said yesterday that after an earlier loss, you pointed to this four game stretch as an opportunity to go 4-0. Why was it important for you at that point to define that goal for this team? >> Well, I think, you know, just the way the, you know, the schedule comes out every year, you can usually probably break it into quarters or trimesters has been my personal experience. Um, I think when you chart, you know, your schedule, you know, there's training. Um, you know, how do you look at September, you know, I view September as an extension of training camp, how we train a team. I think October is such a transition month for your team, where you are, the padded work, the fundamentals, or things looking the way. So, I mean, all those things factor and it's all part of the planning. I I I think it's it's under underrated uh for what a head coach brings to a program. You know, I I've always felt that how you schedule your team, how you train your team, you know, the internal resources balanced with the external resources, that's that's all part of the equation of creating the environment and we everybody throws the word buzzword culture on it, but it's it's so much deeper uh in that with you know what culture truly means, but your structure and your training regiments and scheduling is a huge part of how you operate, the city you live in, the external resources. I mean, this, you know, this is what keeps coaches up late at night. This, I know it does me personally because at the end of the day, you know, you're it's about winning and and creating the environment, the structure for your players to be the best they can be because hopefully it'll be the best they can be for the organization. So uh so with that the simple you know this is called a filibuster so I'm hoping not have to answer one question after this but if you're following along here but no so I think clearly you know breaking up in quarters and trimesters it gives you a chance to plug and play and you know doing it doing it for a long time you have metrics that you can kind of say hey this is where I think I'm at you know compared to way it was you know how many years ago uh because you know the CBA has changed the way you can train the team, you know, so and we're all on an equal playing field there. So, um, you know, it's to me it's part of the chess match of being a head coach. >> So, Mike, what are you learning about your culture, your group through some of these tight wins? >> Yeah, it's great. We need these games, frankly. I mean, trust me, I'd love to win by 21 points every week and and and but you need these games. Uh, uh, I've I've been in I've had an experience of being 15 and one and not having really any close games and then you get to the playoffs and whoa, here you go. and now you're in one. So, um, so, uh, dance those dances, you know, have those memories. Um, I think it's all part of your your journey and and what you can help try to emulate for your team. Um, but close games are are are critical. I mean, Cleveland's won a bunch of close games that, you know, you that pays forward. You know, it's everybody talks about being comfortable, you know, in those moments. you know, it's, you know, everybody trains game management, everybody trains the, you know, those situations, you know, week in and week out going all the way back to the OTAAS. But to have it in live action, you know, the, you know, the the thunder, the rush on field goal for us right at the end of the half, you know, we I can't how many how many times we practice that and our guys bang, they nailed it, you know, it's perfect. So, you have to have those moments in live action. So, um, so with that, I I do I feel like we're we're building confidence. We're we're stacking it. And I do I I I think there's a tremendous amount that comes off of that wind. Um you know, especially on the road, the travel stress, you know, stress is additive, whether it's physical, emotional, mental, that that's that's the reality of life. Uh it's the reality how I feel, how you need to train a team. Um so I love the vibe of our guys. I like the card playing. I like the interaction. I loved everything about the trip, you know, because it wasn't it's not easy for anybody. So um so there's a there's a lot of lot of good that comes out of it and most importantly we won you know that's that's where you can put the stamp on it but you know your preparation is separate from the performance. So I think we all it's human nature to think ah you know I didn't you know we didn't prepare you know right that's why we didn't win the game or we prepared so good why didn't we win the game you know so I think you really got to watch that but if you see things in your preparation during the course week and then they show up on Sunday then that's responsibility us as coaches and that's where I'll kick myself in the ass just say hey I I saw that on Wednesday and I didn't redo it on Thursday types of things so because things can carry you know so you get what you emphasize guys, you know, but I think in today's world, you know, generationally, um, and just just raising children, you you get what you tolerate, too. So, I think you just got to be conscientious of those things as you break seasons into quarters or trimesters or you talk about the importance of close games. Um, you know, all this is very important of of putting together a run and we're trying to complete a four game run right now. That's what we set out to do and um we got a chance to do it, you know, here at home. So, we're we're right where we need to be. Mike, with the get Mike, with uh the guys having off today, how much catchup do you have to play at all this week to get where you need to be by Wednesday? >> I mean, which which >> which you know they usually come or >> Well, >> well, I I think you know just kind of, you know, it's just a uh an example what I just talked about. I mean, you have to factor in the flight, you know, you factor in the you know, that was that was a hard-fought game. Um the flight over, you know, being in a hotel for an extra day or two. So, I mean, [snorts] you know, um, you know, the old adage that, you know, it's one bottle, one bottle of water for every hour you're on the flight. You know, you know, times that by two for every day you're in the hotel. I mean, hydration, you know, talk, everybody says hydrate, sleep. Okay, cool. All right, I'll do that. But, uh, but the specifics of it, you know, we have a great support staff here. I mean, our our people, you know, Gabe and his staff, training staff, you know, I I just I can't say enough about those guys, you know, gals, too. Um, and the training staff. So, that and the players are are buying in. It's no way's the same. You know, everybody does it a little differently. We do it a little differently now. So, um, when you have this opportunity, you go over and, you [snorts] know, you get out on the field and you you say, "Okay, the team's prepared." you know, I felt like we definitely checked the box of what we wanted to get done before that. Um, but it's definitely this week, too. It's not over yet. So, and that's why our Wednesday practice will be very similar to last week. So, we'll treat the beginning of this week similar to how we treated the beginning of last week. >> When we first talked to you, I think one of the things you said you talked about, the big guys on this team will be the first ones off the bus and how impressed you were with the linemen you guys have assembled. You guys are the only offense in the NFL right now that's converted every time you run the ball on third or fourth or two and less. What do you guys >> That sounds like a t-shirt, huh? >> What do you guys do? What do you see them do so well to win at the point of attack? And what goes into preparing to win those situations? >> I mean, it starts with the personnel. It starts starts with the individuals, the men. I I think just, you know, when you get into your first personnel meeting and you you talk about the profile of your players and, you know, our [snorts] D line and O line, they they they look the way they're supposed to look. You know, I you know, I'm not a short guy, but I'm not the tallest guy. You know, when I when I when I walk off the bus, I want to look my guy like this. Sorry about that, but it's trying to make a point here. But, you know, I don't want to look anybody eye. So, I don't want to look anybody that's stalls you. So, but uh I just so that goes to Omar and Art and you know what's what's been done here before I think it's uh it's important. Um so, you know, our length and and all those things, but most importantly the men. I mean, we we got the right we got the right guys. We got a really good mix of veterans, you know, and young guys and you know, you're you're just seeing it come together. You know, our young defensive linemen played well. I mean, they're they're doing some good things. You know, Cam is doing an excellent job, you know, with his leadership and his give back. I think see veterans can give back so much in just the little things that they can say in a one-on-one drill and they what they can say um you know in passing in a weight room you know so in the video component of it uh cuz you know it is it's a lot like parenting you tell your kids something two or three times but you know Fen Rogers or Cam Hayward or TJ says something to them like they act like they never heard before. So, and that's, you know, that that's real. And I just think to give back of our bets has been good and and our young guys are responding and um and I it's it's it's really a challenge every year that that I've been doing this. You look at your veterans and your young guys and that that cavern that's between them and you you see it come together and you know and it's it's important to do that and win. You know, you got to win while you do it. But, uh you know, we our young guys are playing some snaps and and they're contributing. So, you know, the next step is it's got to show up on special teams. You know, that that's a little bit of our, you know, challenge right now. We need to get more production out of our special teams and we'll just keep working the fundamentals, keep emphasizing it and and I believe that, you know, that that'll get to where it needs to be. >> Mike, growing up in Pittsburgh as you did and rooting for the Steelers as you did. Does coaching against their arch rival mean anything extra to you or is it just another game? >> Absolutely. Um, I mean, Cleveland is, you know, if you grow up here, you you think, you know, you I was I'll be I was shocked the first time I went to Cleveland cuz it it it looked like nothing I was told it looked like. You know, it's they have nice suburbs. They got a good downtown and, you know, but the impression of, you know, of what you think of the Cleveland Browns in Cleveland as a kid is is different. So, yeah, I I enjoyed I remember the the great rivalries in in the old days, the cardiac kids, and, you know, the history of it, too. So, um, that's cool. Um, when I do bring it up, I don't I don't think some of the guys even know what the hell I'm talking about if I bring up the cardiac kids. But, so, and you know, some of the some of those some of those years, but you know, this is a this is a new era and they got a new coach and uh, we have a new coach. Um, so, you know, we had our first game together up here in Cleveland. It was a it was a tough battle and so I'm looking forward to getting it on again. What do you think of that loss? What are a couple of things that have to go differently for you guys to swim the outcome in your favor? >> Oh, I just think that just to, you know, build off of where we are today. Let's not lose sight of what we've accomplished, you know, the last [snorts] three weeks. Um, recognize what they've done, you know, the last, you know, every how many weeks when they have four or five, you know, victories coming back in the fourth quarter. So just recognizing those specifics of, you know, what's being done, how they're doing, and but at the end of the day, you know, we need to play to our play style, you know, play to to everything we believe in the specifics of it, and and our performance will be where it needs to be to win the game. >> What you were saying earlier about, you know, the big guys of the team, you inherited this roster, you saw, you know, guys like Kean, Zack, Troy, Derek, guys that have, you know, been developing but were still young and developing. Uh you know, we first start from the personnel department. I I think clearly u you know, defensively playing the 34 defense here since 1992. um you know having an understanding of what the outside linebacker position is and and and [snorts] how you draft for it. No one's done it better. I mean it's you know history shows you that repeatedly here. So and that's still in place. Um the inside pieces you know with the length you know and and Ken, you know Cam and Derek and you know KB all those guys reflect that. Um so you know they're big men you know big men with length. So the profiles definitely has been in place here, you know, up front and offensive line just, you know, you look at the draft capital that's, you know, in place. You know, that's why it was so important to take Max, you know, and and the way that worked out with Max, it's it's he belongs here. You know, he's what he's what a Pittsburgh Steeler [snorts] offensive tackle looks like. You know, he has the ability to play right or left in today's game. So we, you know, we don't just draft the left tackle profile, the right tackle profile, which was done at one time in my career. I mean, those guys, um, no one does it better in the front. You know, Patrick, you know, his origin is, you know, defensive front linebacker so far. started off as an offensive line coach which I which I love that about him and his in his journey and you know as we've talked football over you know over time and and James Camp and I think he's the best O line coach in the league you know and and felt that way for decades. So um so yes all that but the end of the day you know it's the the players got to buy in and you know and have an understanding that this thing's set for them to be the big brothers. They're the big brothers of our football team. You know, you know, it hits the fan, they they're in the front, you know, then let's get it on. So, you know, what a better team to do than than the Cleveland. So, this this will be great game for us to take a step forward as a team. You know, win this game, get to six and two and and win up front. You know, we went into Paris and said that uh we need to own the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. We did it. What allowed for some of the results we saw from the middle linebackers yesterday? >> What said >> what what allowed I mean what what were they they doing well or what were people around? I think uh just you know we're growing. We're growing through our menus. You know I thought uh Patrick Graham did an excellent job and I thought PQ had a excellent week and frankly we cut him loose on some pressures early. You know activate them and you know G gave him a little more um ownership in what exactly what we're doing and and um you know the play caller meetings and and the things that are going on. So yeah, you definitely see growth of Peyton's plays has been probably one of the biggest plays in the game. You know clearly I mean that's a big time play on a 8 n 10 play drive. So yeah, I just think those guys are stepping forward and you're just you're just seeing us getting connected and I think the upkick and pressure has has benefited us too and I think we all recognize that. >> Mike, how do you evaluate how Deshawn Elliott played in his first regular season game back in nearly a year? >> Was great.
