title: Matthew Stafford Just Made NFL History & We May NEVER See It Again
text: Joining us now, ladies and gentlemen, is the number one overall pick from the 2009 draft. Now the all-time leader in passing touchdowns in two different franchises. What a stallion. Ladies and gentlemen, Super Bowl champion, MVP, Matthew Stafford. >> Fellas, how we doing? >> Dude, thank you for joining us. So thankful that you made time. I understand you're fresh out of breaking some franchise records and there's a lot going on. So we appreciate we were surprised. Okay? I was I just mentioned I think you heard me talk about that. But how has this era of being an LA Ram I I think a lot of people whenever you go out there with what your age was naturally, you win a Super Bowl, then there was like he's going to retire, he's going to retire. And then how would we recall it? Now you're the all-time leader for the Rams. Does that carry any more weight for you as like the face of two franchises? Like how do you kind of view your experience in Los Angeles now? >> Yeah, I I kind of look back at the kind of the same way you guys do. I sit there and go, man, I have been here for a little bit and I do have so much respect for the guys that played the position before me. Obviously passing Roman Gabriel is a really cool thing for me. Being a kid just loving the history of this game and being able to be in the same breath as guys like that means a lot to me. I think about it and I think about all the teammates I got to throw to. You guys always say remember launching touchdowns to Calvin Johnson and Pedigrew and all the boys in in Detroit you know, when we were all still playing and and now I sit there and think you know, I'm throwing them to Davante Adams and and Puka Nacua. It's it's a special thing to be a part of. A lot of people had their hand in it. I don't catch them. I just throw them, but there's a lot of people out there that make those things happen. So just appreciative to be able to play this long and and loving my time here for sure. >> Tell me a little bit about McVay's offense and why you have loved it so much since day one. It does feel like you two are a great tag team. I know contract there was some stuff, but on the field and I believe as friends you two work magic together. Why is that? What what is it about the way McVay operates that you love so much? >> Yeah, you know, I think we challenge each other. You know, he's obviously challenged me in you know, on the field asked me to do things that I was never asked to really do in Detroit where that's moving the pocket or doing some of the things we do within the offense. And then I think in the same breath, I bring things that I'm used to doing when I was in Detroit, um, you know, to where hey, let's let's mold these two things together. Let's try to find a way to be the best that we can. And we're all ultimately out there just trying to be problem solvers, right? Uh, week in and week out there's injuries, things that happen throughout the game. How are we going to find a way to win the ball game? And and I've just loved being in the foxhole with him. He's been in my ear since I've been here and uh, love going to battle with him. >> I don't know what the percentage is, but it feels like every other throw you have you don't see who you're throwing it to. AJ has a question about that actually, Matty. >> Matthew, obviously your your no-look stuff gets a lot of attention, which it should because it's a it's an absolute weapon. I know we've had Aaron Rodgers on here complimenting you on your no-look passes. Like, how did that come about? Was that something that just started as a joke or you're messing around playing with your buddies? Like, is it something you can work on in practice? And and I guess did you expect to be doing it this often? >> Yeah, no, I don't I don't think I don't think I really ever expected to be doing it this often. I think it really started, uh, to be honest with you, AJ, back when we were battling against each other and everybody in the building knew I was trying to throw it to Calvin. So, okay, how do I, you know, not look at Calvin and still throw it to Calvin? Um, you know, that was kind of how it started and then, you know, I think, uh, with the way that coach, um, allows me to have some freedom here, um, just tried to know what the defense is doing. Hey, I know what we're doing on offense. I'm trying to find ways to make a good play better or a play that might be a little bit uphill, make it work. And so, uh, it's it's a natural thing. It doesn't I don't think about it before the snap. I catch the ball. Um, I I understand what the defense is in. I try to move guys if I need to move guys. And sometimes you don't, but, um, you know, one one yesterday tried to peel a corner off of a flat route for us and and it ended up working and uh, we scored a touchdown on it. So, uh, I'm happy to do them when they work. When they don't, uh, that's a tough feeling. But, uh, it worked, uh, most of the time. >> Yeah, I'm trying to get a guy off a guy, you know, just got I'm I'm letting the eyes dance, just seeing whenever he can move and then do it. And that do you work How often are you working that? Like in practice, are you working that every day or is this just a natural ability? And do you think future quarterbacks should be forced to learn how to do this? >> [laughter] >> No, I think you should only do it if you know Aaron's been doing it more now. I'll tell you what, he does some you know, a lot of times looking straight throwing out to his right. I see him checking them down doing some of those throws down there giving his guys a little bit more room which is is an impressive impressive deal too. But no, it comes up in practice for sure. I don't think about it like I said and it comes up it comes up organically in practice as well. It's not like hey, here's the play I'm going to no look it. Let's go do it. It just happens and it's a fun little right of passage for the linebackers that we're practicing against if we get a new guy in try to get him moving one way throw behind him one day and just tip of the cap to him. He looks back to me like what the hell is that? But it's it's a lot of fun. >> Yeah, he the rest of the defense too. >> Poor kids get cut. Kids jump in the crosshairs >> Hey, welcome to the Rams, bud. You don't know who Matthew Stafford is, you [ __ ] idiot. You think he's going to look where he's throwing it? Yeah, right. That is a hilarious realization in real time I would assume for him. D-Butt has a question for you. You guys are supposed to be undefeated and you're supposed to win MVP again. Go ahead, D-Butt. >> Yeah, obviously it's a play-to-play week-to-week league, you know, inside that locker room but outside noise coming in that those were the expectations with you coming back as a reigning MVP, Miles Garrett coming over reigning Defensive Player of the Year and obviously Sean McVay being who he is. How's it been managing the expectations in that locker room even from the preseason now where you sit going forward? >> Yeah, I think it's been a big challenge. Obviously, the biggest thing is is trying to be as steady as I possibly can when when things, you know, aren't going your way. We've played a couple games this year where we feel like we played well enough to win them. For one reason or another, we haven't you know, come away with those victories and that's a tough pill to swallow as you guys know when you feel like you got a game, you know, and it doesn't go your way at the end. That's difficult. But at the same time, how steady can I be so the guys that haven't been through some of the storms that an NFL season inevitably bring? Hey, how can I be steady for those guys so they look at me and go, "Okay, we're going to be all right. Look how Stafford's acting. Let's go." And and I'm really proud of the work of the week of work that we had last week that led to a great game. Um we got to go keep keep doing that. You know, we got to stack uh stack those weeks on top of each other so that we can uh get where we want to be. >> I don't know if you've heard all of us talk about your team. Uh last week on Monday Night Countdown on this show, I think on NFL Live, I think everybody that speaks about your team. Are we worried about the Rams? You know, because the way records are in math and like how often teams have been able to go on. All of us have a like an unwavering and unflappable belief in you guys. Just because the amount of talent you have. I assume same for you guys. I assume the same for you guys. >> Yeah, but I would say less so because of our talent probably a little bit more so because of our resilience. You know, I think uh a couple years ago, 2023, I believe it was, we were one and four to start the season, made the playoffs. We were three and six the next year, made the playoffs. Um you know, we'd love to come out and and start like we did in 2021 and be seven and one or whatever it was to start the season, but you know, you go through storms in an NFL season. Sometimes that's, you know, right out the gate. And so uh we got to find a way to come out of that thing, find our identity, make sure that we're playing good football, and and yesterday was a step in the right in the right direction. Still some plays out there that we wish we had back. And and if we can clean those up, it'll look even better. So uh just happy to get a win. As we move forward, continue to try to get better um as the season goes. >> We love watching your team, and we feel like the uh story of this NFL season, 13 personnel, which we're going to ask you about here in a bit cuz you have a triple tower type situation, but the run game seemingly more important now in ball than it has been for the last couple of decades. Connor has a question for you about that, Staff. >> Yeah, Matthew, having both Akers and Kyren Williams back there seemingly huge for for the offense and something that maybe you've never had before when it comes to kind of a two-headed monster back there. How awesome is it to have those two guys? And how often now do you go up there with a run play call or a pass play called, and you're like, you know what, I'm just going to check it cuz both my running backs are unbelievable. >> Yeah, they are. It's it's a whole lot of fun. Um and you're right. I haven't had a uh tandem like this where they both can do everything, right? You usually have one big guy, one small guy, a big slow guy that can run over people, and a small fast guy that can run around people, and and this is a really unique instance in which we can call our entire offense with both those guys in the game and not not bat an eye. Sometimes I get in the huddle, I don't know which one of them's in the damn game. They look so much alike anyways. So, hey, we just go out there and play ball, and and those guys do what they do, but it is fun. And I know our guys up front love blocking in the run game for those guys cuz they're making big plays, and and uh you know, that's that's when football is fun, when everybody's getting involved. Both backs are touching it. Um the old lineman are getting after it. Um yesterday was a fun experience. >> Yeah, so when the run game gets going, obviously, you can, you know, we can start cooking a little bit. And then that sucks up the line back. We're trying to suck them up. Trying to get them sucked up. You know who eats? They had a holiday yesterday. Diggs has a question for you, Staff. >> Yeah, I do. And and there was a lot made last year about, I don't know, halfway through the season, you guys went to a ton of 12, 13 personnel, and Pat was out there for Monday night, and he's like, you guys need to see these tight ends in person. They're like all 6'8, they're all like 250, and they can all run. So, how do you choose each week who which tight end's going to get two touchdowns in we each week, and how fun is it having those guys uh available for you? >> It's a it's a blast. We pick straws. Um and >> uh you know, I was happy for DA. We call him the general. Uh that's why everybody was saluting him afterwards, but uh uh he uh he he drew the the straw this week. So, you know, [laughter] I just tried to feed him down there in the red zone. Next week, it'll be somebody else. No, it is it's so much fun to play with those guys. You know, like you said, they're all big, tall, strong, fast, can do it all, complete football players, uh but great teammates, too, man. They all celebrate each other, which is a whole hell of a lot of fun to be around. When guys can be happy for other people's success, you've been on teams like that where, you know, a guy scores and everybody's juiced for him, no matter what, even if they play the same position. So, happy to have those guys and and they definitely make it go for us. >> That's great to hear, especially with the rocky start not rocky start you guys had. You know, cuz people can turn on each other. Instead, it sounds like you guys have only hunkered down and started celebrating each other more. Here's a stat from Sarah Barshop, per ESPN research, you guys ran a season-high 34 plays with three tight ends on the field. Also had a season-high 38 rushes. I kind of said this earlier, it was our top five headline number five, the pound the rock era. Does it feel like it's more bigger bodies again, like maybe at the beginning of your career in the NFL as opposed to what it became on the field at all times? >> Yeah, absolutely. I I definitely think so. This feels, uh, you know, around the league when you look at it, um, fullbacks are back, um, you know, tight ends are back. This is what it felt like when I came into the league, like you said, in 2009. Um, you know, it's cyclical, everything kind of goes in a circle and then it became a huge 11 personnel nickel defense league for a long, long time. Um, and and now it feels like we're kind of coming back to it. So, uh, got to ride the wave, got to figure out what works and and obviously whatever personnel group you got out there, you got to go out there and execute and get it done. But, uh, it was nice to get the big fellows on the field yesterday, pound the rock a little bit and uh, usually when you have 38 rushes, means you're leading the game, you're doing things the right way. So, happy to happy to be doing that. >> Yeah, and you got wide receivers that'll run through somebody's face, too. And I know you're happy to get Oos back. Ty has a question for you. >> Yeah, Matthew, how has your relationship with uh, Puka evolved since he got there? I guess I think it was the Monday night game where he had, you know, 17 catches, set a whole bunch of records. And I assume, you know, yes, you guys ran the ball a bunch, but with Davante being out for a little bit here, have you pulled Puka aside and been like, "Hey, I don't know how much you watched when I was in Detroit, but I'm going to be throwing you the ball 30 to 35 times a game. So, I'm going to need you, you know, really locked in for these next several weeks." >> No, I didn't have to say anything to him. That guy knows he's getting the rock. He's he's a heck of a football player. Another guy on our team that everybody loves. Love to be around him. What he brings to our team energy-wise on game days is incredible. Like he said, running through people's face. He's the physical player at the you know receiver position that I've ever been around. And that's that's when he catches it and runs it but I mean I bet people miss blocks where he's going through the hole and he really has the safety but the linebacker shows up and he just goes ahead and knocks that guy down too. So I mean he's he's a special player. We're happy to have him but I think all those guys know when Davante, a player like that, a Hall of Famer, future Hall of Famer, you know, goes down it's going to be all hands on deck and those guys stepped up in a big way yesterday. >> You're the man. We appreciate you joining us. Congrats on all the success. Good luck the rest of the way. We can't wait to watch you continue to do your thing. And congrats on another record, dude. You're going to means you're old but congrats on another record. >> Appreciate [applause] it, fellas. Always fun to come on with you guys. >> You're the man. Ladies and gentlemen, that's NFL MVP Matthew Stafford. >> Yeah, Matthew. >> That's the only way you get those records. You got to be old, you know. You got to be around a long time. I like that he was just as surprised as us. Man, I can have the all-time leader over here? It feels like I just got here yesterday. It does feel like it was yesterday but I guess he's been very prolific since the day he arrived as a Los Angeles Ram. AJ, playing against Matthew Stafford, his arm talent always there. Just a ridiculous toughness about him. Yeah, a competitor. Yeah, exactly. I think that is his big thing. Don't you think, AJ? >> Yeah, it's the the combination of the relentless competitor that wants to win at all costs. Like we'll we'll play through anything but also the physical tools. I mean that's why he's the number one overall pick. When you have a guy that can have both like we know a lot of guys Pat like that are physical freaks. Like they have all the tools but they just can't seem to put it together. They don't have the drive or the competitiveness whatever whatever it it Matthew's one of those guys I think that has both. He's the combo that will compete to the death, but he also has the physical tools and wants to win more than anybody. So, yeah, I was I guess unlucky enough to see that firsthand for a long time when I was in Green Bay playing against him, but also like had so much respect for the dude watching him do it. Now, when you see him doing it now though, he's not The dude's not slowing down at all. Like his arm strength is off the charts. The all the different arm angles and the platforms that like he throws from. Like he's still doing it all. I don't think he should He should not stop anytime soon. >> I don't like that photo right there for Matthew Stafford. You know, he's got a can there. He's got bad tan line there, but he still looks unbelievable. But, >> D- But, I want to ask you about this. A lot of these older quarterbacks, their arms become noodles. I mean, it's happened. We We've Drew Brees said he wasn't strong enough to come back whenever everybody wanted him to come back. Matt Ryan at the end of his career like his arm just couldn't do it anymore. Philip Rivers, I think he was like, "I can't get it." At some point your arm just like kickers or punters, it happens where you just don't have enough explosiveness to be able to do what you do. Matthew Stafford and Aaron, the old guard as we wrap up headline number four here, they're still throwing it just as good as they did 10 years ago. It doesn't make sense. It kind of defies what's supposed to happen, D- But. >> Yeah, some of these guys, they'll be able to throw the ball forever. Like Aaron Rodgers, whether Dan Marino could probably still throw the ball 60 yards in the air. Joe Flacco, he's a guy who just has a gun for an arm. So, Matt Stafford is one of those guys. And then once he got to the Rams, he mentioned it like it was just a different evolution that he had to take with the run game, with the play action game, with moving the pocket. So, you have a guy that can drop back and throw it 60 times, and you're in trouble as a defense. Now, when you give him a run game and a play action game to draft to worry about, it can become unstoppable. Now, injuries have have been a part of some of the things that gotten in their way, but the efficiency from them like they were five for five in the red area, I believe, against the Raiders. He's just He's unbelievable. And as his mind is kind of sped up, his body and his arm haven't slowed down. So, yeah, that's a great, great combination for a quarterback. >> Combination. Good for Matthew Stafford. The combination of two all-time leading passers for two different franchises. Super Bowl champ and an MVP. That's first ballot, we think. >> Could be. >> Got to be. >> We We think. >> [music]
